# Region protocol

<!-- Generated from contracts/protocol.json; DO NOT EDIT. -->

[한국어](protocol.ko.md).

This document defines the application manifest, routing, rendering, the requests and responses between a hyper server and the hyper browser code, and the two rendering modes. The server can render the first document as HTML (server-side rendering, SSR), or a static shell can render it in the browser (client-side rendering, CSR). Template syntax and rendering rules are defined by the template language; this document does not change them.

## Application manifest

- **HY-1** <a id="HY-1.1"></a> An application declares its structure in one JSON file, the manifest. <a id="HY-1.2"></a> Server and browser read the same manifest.

```json
{
  "layout": "layout.tpl",
  "title": "title.tpl",
  "regions": [
    { "name": "left", "template": "left.tpl", "uses": ["posts", "path"] },
    { "name": "content", "page": true }
  ],
  "routes": [
    { "name": "board.list", "path": "/board", "title": "Board", "template": "board/list.tpl", "regions": [{ "name": "rows", "template": "board/rows.tpl" }] },
    { "name": "board.create", "path": "/board/create", "title": "Write", "template": "board/create.tpl", "post": true },
    { "name": "board.show", "path": "/board/{id}", "title": "Post", "template": "board/show.tpl",
      "representations": [{ "type": "application/vnd.example.post+json", "parameters": { "version": ["1"] }, "methods": ["GET", "PUT"], "vary": ["Authorization"] }] }
  ]
}
```

- **HY-2** <a id="HY-2.1"></a> `regions` and `routes` are ordered lists. <a id="HY-2.2"></a> Region names and route names are strings and are unique. <a id="HY-2.3"></a> A region name matches `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*` and is not `layout`, `title`, `data` or `build`. <a id="HY-2.4"></a> Exactly one region has `"page": true` and no `template`; every other region has a `template` and a list of used topics. <a id="HY-2.5"></a> A route with `"post": true` accepts a `POST` action. <a id="HY-2.6"></a> A route may declare `representations` (HY-118). <a id="HY-2.7"></a> A server checks its manifest against these rules when it starts, and the asset build checks the manifest before it writes the client bundle; the browser does not check the manifest of its bundle again.

- **HY-3** <a id="HY-3.1"></a> The layout renders the title definition inside `<title>` with `{# title}`, the data definition with `{# data}` (HY-31), the build definition with `{# build}` inside `<head>` (HY-125), and each region with `{# name}` inside an element whose `id` is the region name, for example `<main id="content">{# content}</main>`. <a id="HY-3.2"></a> A region placement has no block arguments. <a id="HY-3.3"></a> The browser finds a region element by its `id`; no other marker exists.

## Routing

- **HY-4** <a id="HY-4.1"></a> A route path starts with `/`. <a id="HY-4.2"></a> The segments after it are separated by `/`. <a id="HY-4.3"></a> A segment is either a literal of the characters `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -` or a parameter `{name}` where `name` matches `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`. <a id="HY-4.4"></a> The path `/` has no segments. <a id="HY-4.6"></a> The router refuses a route path against this rule or HY-49, such as one that repeats a parameter name, so an application whose manifest declares it fails to open.

- **HY-5** <a id="HY-5.1"></a> A request path matches a route when it starts with `/`, has the same number of segments, every literal segment is equal to the request segment byte for byte, and every parameter segment is non-empty. <a id="HY-5.2"></a> The query string is not part of the path. <a id="HY-5.3"></a> The parameters of a match are a map from each parameter name to its value, in the order of the parameters in the route path.

- **HY-6** <a id="HY-6.1"></a> A parameter value is the request segment with every `%XX` sequence (two hexadecimal digits) decoded to its byte. <a id="HY-6.2"></a> A segment with a `%` that is not followed by two hexadecimal digits, or whose decoded bytes are not valid UTF-8, does not match.

- **HY-7** <a id="HY-7.1"></a> Routes are tried in manifest order, and the first route that matches is the result. <a id="HY-7.2"></a> A path that matches no route has no result.

- **HY-8** <a id="HY-8.1"></a> An application may run under a base path such as `/api`. <a id="HY-8.2"></a> A request path is routed after removing the base path; a request path that does not start with the base path followed by `/` or the end of the path has no result. <a id="HY-8.3"></a> `Location` headers include the base path.

- **HY-49** <a id="HY-49.1"></a> The last segment of a route path may be a rest parameter `{name*}`, with `name` as in HY-4 and different from the other parameters of the path. <a id="HY-49.2"></a> It stands at zero or more remaining request segments and matches when every one of them is empty or decodes by HY-6. <a id="HY-49.3"></a> Its value is the rest of the request path without decoding: `/` followed by the remaining segments joined with `/`, or `/` when none remains.

## Data and topics

- **HY-10** <a id="HY-10.1"></a> Shared data is one map that the layout, the title and every region receive. <a id="HY-10.2"></a> It starts with `title`, the route title, and `csrf`, the masked session token of HY-24 for this response, then `context`, the context of the application (HY-124), when the application declares one, followed by the values that the application adds. <a id="HY-10.3"></a> When the read paths of the route (HY-73) remove `csrf`, `context` comes right after `title`, and when they remove both, it comes first; placing the context in shared data that already holds a member `context` fails, with HY-43 on a server and with an error in the browser, because the context has one place and one source.

- **HY-11** <a id="HY-11.1"></a> Every non-page region declares the topics it uses. <a id="HY-11.2"></a> A topic names data that can change, such as `posts`. <a id="HY-11.3"></a> The topic `path` is built in: it changes when the request path differs from the path of the `HX-Current-URL` request header after removing the base path.

## Rendering

- **HY-12** <a id="HY-12.1"></a> A document is the layout rendered with root data equal to the shared data and with `html` definitions: `title` (the title rendered alone), `data` (HY-31), `build` (HY-125) and one per manifest region, the region rendered alone. <a id="HY-12.2"></a> The page region template is the route template.

- **HY-13** <a id="HY-13.1"></a> A region rendered alone uses the region template and the root data `merge(shared, region data)`, where a region data value replaces a shared value with the same name. <a id="HY-13.2"></a> The page region receives every route region of its route, rendered alone, as an `html` definition. <a id="HY-13.3"></a> The title rendered alone uses the title template and the shared data. <a id="HY-13.4"></a> The server and the browser compose documents and region parts in this same way, so they produce the same bytes. <a id="HY-13.5"></a> A document or a region response binds each of its roots once with the bound map of the template engine (VAL-22): the shared data, the data of every region and, in a document that embeds its data, the embedded data (HY-31). <a id="HY-13.6"></a> Every render of the response uses those bound maps and `merge`, so the number of binds does not grow with the number of renders; a shared value is bound in the shared data and once more in the embedded data of a document that embeds its data, because the embedded data carries the shared data.

- **HY-14** <a id="HY-14.1"></a> Server and browser render with the same environment. <a id="HY-14.2"></a> The server sends the time zone in every JSON response.

- **HY-48** <a id="HY-48.1"></a> A server renders documents and regions as HY-12 and HY-13 define, with the template engine of its runtime, from the outputs of the build (HR-96): the manifest, the templates of the application, the read paths `reads.json` (HY-73) and the build id `build.json` (HY-125). <a id="HY-48.2"></a> It opens the application only when every output that it needs exists: `open` fails with the absolute path of the first missing output, so that a missing build fails when the application opens and names the missing file. <a id="HY-48.3"></a> The build first rejects `hx-*` attributes outside the layout (HC-6 of the [application authoring rules](../operations/composition.md)) and checks the templates with the rules of HY-3 (with the placement `{# build}`, HY-125), HY-30 and HY-75, the same rules as `make templates-check`, and a violation fails the build with every problem before it removes or writes any output, so a server program never serves templates that break them.

  - <a id="HY-48.4"></a> PHP: PHP renders with a program that the build compiles from the application templates: with the generated PHP program of the same templates, through the API of the template package, which the native template extension `polyspec_template` registers under the same names when PHP has loaded it, so that the server holds no branch on the extension. <a id="HY-48.5"></a> The program passes the same tests and `make parity` with and without the extension. <a id="HY-48.6"></a> The build compiles the generated program into a PHP namespace that the application chooses and writes it into the directory `php` of the program directory as PSR-4 files, one class per file named after its class, so it declares no global name and the programs of several applications load in one PHP process. <a id="HY-48.7"></a> The application maps that namespace to that directory in `autoload.psr-4` of its `composer.json`, and the server takes the class `GeneratedProgram` of the namespace that `program.json` names through the autoload of Composer and requires no file of the program itself. <a id="HY-48.8"></a> `App::open` fails when the program directory has no directory `php`, no `program.json`, no `reads.json` (HY-73), no `build.json` (HY-125) or no directory `templates`, with the absolute path of the first missing one. <a id="HY-48.9"></a> It also fails when the autoload does not load that class, naming the class and the directory `php` that `autoload.psr-4` must map to its namespace.
  - <a id="HY-48.10"></a> Python: the program directory holds `reads.json`, `build.json` and the directory `templates`; `App.open` fails with a `ValueError` (HY-106) that names the first missing one.
  - <a id="HY-48.11"></a> Node: `App.open` reads the manifest, the template index, the template files and the build id file by absolute paths, the last from its option `build`, the absolute path of the `build.json` of the asset output (HY-125); a missing file fails with the error that names its path.

## Requests

- **HY-15** <a id="HY-15.1"></a> A request that selects `application/vnd.hyper+json` (HY-116) and has `HX-Request: true`, which htmx sends with every request, is a region request; one that selects it without `HX-Request` is a document request. <a id="HY-15.2"></a> A request that selects `text/html` is an HTML request and receives an HTML document. <a id="HY-15.3"></a> A JSON response has `Content-Type: application/vnd.hyper+json`. <a id="HY-15.4"></a> A region request always updates the page region (HY-18). <a id="HY-15.5"></a> `application/json` is not a media type of hyper, so an application can give it its own meaning in a representation (HY-118).

- **HY-56** <a id="HY-56.1"></a> The raw query of a request is the request target after its first `?` up to its first `#`, or empty text without a `?`. <a id="HY-56.2"></a> Its values are read without nesting: the raw query is split at every `&` and an empty part is skipped; the name of a part is the text before its first `=` and the value is the rest, or empty text when the part has no `=`; in both, `+` is a space, `%XX` with two hexadecimal digits is its byte and any other `%` stays. <a id="HY-56.3"></a> A name with brackets, such as `roles[]` or `a[b]`, is the name as written, and an empty name is a name. <a id="HY-56.4"></a> The query values are an ordered map from each name, in the order of its first occurrence, to the list of its values in request order; a name or value that is not valid UTF-8 fails with HY-42. <a id="HY-56.5"></a> `Request` provides the raw query and the query values, and `queryInt` reads the last value of a name.

- **HY-57** <a id="HY-57.1"></a> The form values of a request are read from its raw body without nesting, as an ordered map like the query values of HY-56. <a id="HY-57.2"></a> An `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body is read as the raw query is. <a id="HY-57.3"></a> A `multipart/form-data` body gives one value for each part whose `Content-Disposition` is `form-data` with a `name` parameter and no `filename` parameter: the name is that parameter and the value is the content of the part as it is; a part with a `filename` is a file and not a form value. <a id="HY-57.4"></a> A body of another type has no form values. <a id="HY-57.5"></a> A name or value that is not valid UTF-8 fails with HY-42. <a id="HY-57.6"></a> The PHP server reads the body from `php://input`, not from `$_POST`, which nests bracketed names; PHP gives it the body of a `multipart/form-data` request only when `enable_post_data_reading` is off. <a id="HY-57.7"></a> `Request` provides the form values, and `formString` reads the last value of a name.

- **HY-113** <a id="HY-113.1"></a> A file part of a `multipart/form-data` body is a part whose `Content-Disposition` is `form-data` with both a `name` parameter and a `filename` parameter (HY-57). <a id="HY-113.2"></a> The request gives its files as `files()`, an ordered map from each name to the list of its files in request order, as HY-57 orders the form values, and `file(name)` returns the last file of a name, or nothing when it has none, as `formString` reads the last value. <a id="HY-113.3"></a> A file has four parts: its name, which is the `name` parameter; its filename, which is the `filename` parameter with the backslash escapes of its quoted string undone and no further decoding; its content type, which is the value of its `Content-Type` header as sent, or the empty text when it has none; and its bytes, which are the content of the part as it is. <a id="HY-113.4"></a> A file with an empty filename is still a file. <a id="HY-113.5"></a> The name, the filename and the content type must be valid UTF-8, and a part that is not gives status 400 as HY-42 does for a name. <a id="HY-113.6"></a> A part without a `name` parameter is neither a form value nor a file, and no rule gives it to the application. <a id="HY-113.7"></a> `filename*` (RFC 5987) is not read. <a id="HY-113.8"></a> The file API is part of the public API of HY-106, in each runtime form: PHP `Request::files()` and `Request::file()` with the file class `UploadedFile`, Python `files()` and `file()` with the class `UploadedFile`, and Node `files()` and `file()` with the type `UploadedFile`.

- **HY-114** <a id="HY-114.1"></a> The application may declare a file limit, the largest number of bytes of one file (HY-113), as an option of the application next to the body limit (HY-59). <a id="HY-114.2"></a> The default is 8 MiB, the same as the default body limit. <a id="HY-114.3"></a> An application that declares no file limit uses the smaller of 8 MiB and its body limit as its file limit, so that it opens with any body limit and refuses a file only when the body limit already refuses its request. <a id="HY-114.4"></a> The check of a declared file limit below applies only to a declared value. <a id="HY-114.5"></a> The reason for the limit is that every runtime holds a file in memory as one value. <a id="HY-114.6"></a> A file limit that is not a positive integer, or that is larger than the body limit, fails when the application opens, as HY-59 states for another limit. <a id="HY-114.7"></a> After the checks of HY-59.4 and HY-59.7 and before any action or `/_hyper/keep` handler runs, the server checks the bytes of each file part of the request: a file whose bytes are more than the file limit makes the request fail with status 413 and the text `Content Too Large`, as HY-59.4 does, and no action runs. <a id="HY-114.8"></a> The server never truncates a file and never passes part of one; a file within the limit is passed whole.

## Media types and representations

A route has one resource and one or more representations of it (RFC 9110, section 3.2): its page as `text/html`, its page data as `application/vnd.hyper+json`, and the media types that it declares. hyper selects the representation, checks the request and writes the response of every one of them, so that an application serves a JSON contract for other clients through the same router, the same limits and the same response rules as its pages.

- **HY-116** <a id="HY-116.1"></a> The server selects the media type of every request, except `<base path>/_hyper/keep` (HY-40), among `text/html`, `application/vnd.hyper+json` and the representation types of its route (HY-118), after the selection of HY-62, the removal of the data base path of a chosen request (HY-62.19) and the routing of the path (HY-27, 404), because the types depend on the route. <a id="HY-116.2"></a> It selects once, and the request holds the selected type and, for a representation, its parameter values; the request kinds of HY-15, the request methods that report them, and every later step read them from the request and do not read `Accept` again. <a id="HY-116.3"></a> A request without `Accept` is read as `Accept: */*` (RFC 9110, section 12.5.1). <a id="HY-116.4"></a> Several `Accept` field lines are one value joined with `, ` (RFC 9110, section 5.3). <a id="HY-116.5"></a> An `Accept` value that does not follow the grammar of RFC 9110, section 12.5.1, or that has a weight that is not a qvalue (section 12.4.2), such as `q=1.5` or `q=x`, receives status 400 with the text `Bad Request`; an empty `Accept` is an empty list, which matches no type. <a id="HY-116.6"></a> Types, subtypes, parameter names and `q` compare without regard to case. <a id="HY-116.7"></a> The server gives each type the weight of the most specific `Accept` range that matches it (the type with its parameters, then the type, then `type/*`, then `*/*`), and a weight of 0 makes the type not acceptable. <a id="HY-116.8"></a> A declared type takes its weight only from the ranges that match it by HY-119, the one of highest weight among them; `type/*`, `*/*` and a range without its required parameters give it no weight. <a id="HY-116.9"></a> `q` is a weight, not a parameter, and what follows it in a range is an accept extension, which hyper does not define and does not read. <a id="HY-116.10"></a> `text/html` and `application/vnd.hyper+json` have no parameters, and a range that names one of them matches it whatever its other parameters, at the specificity of the type; among several such ranges the one of highest weight gives the weight. <a id="HY-116.11"></a> The server takes the type of the highest weight, and among equal weights the first in the order `text/html`, `application/vnd.hyper+json`, then the declared order. <a id="HY-116.12"></a> It then checks the method against the selected type: `methods` for a representation (HY-121), HY-27 for a page. <a id="HY-116.13"></a> A request that matches none of the types receives status 406 with `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `Vary: Accept` and a body that lists the types that its path serves, each on a line that ends with a line feed, in the order `text/html`, `application/vnd.hyper+json` and the declared order; a declared type is listed once for each combination of one served value of every required parameter, ordered by the values of the first parameter of `parameters`, then of the next, and written as the `Content-Type` of HY-119. <a id="HY-116.14"></a> Under a chosen request of HY-62, the path of HY-62.19 serves no `text/html` and the path of HY-62.22 serves only `text/html`. <a id="HY-116.15"></a> A representation is answered only under the data base path (HY-62.19); a request of HY-62.22 receives the 404 and the 405 of HY-62.23 before the selection, so a request of HY-62.22 with a method other than `GET` receives 405 also when no type of the route is acceptable.

- **HY-117** <a id="HY-117.1"></a> A response with `text/html` or `application/vnd.hyper+json` has `Vary: Accept, HX-Request, HX-Current-URL`, followed by `, Hyper-Context` when the application declares a context (HY-124); the shell of HY-62 has the same `Vary`. <a id="HY-117.2"></a> Every response that a representation request receives after the selection, which are the 405, 415 and 400 of HY-121, the response of its handler and its 304 (HY-122) and the 404 and 412 of HY-107, has `Vary: Accept` followed by the `vary` names of its entry (HY-118). <a id="HY-117.3"></a> The 400 and the 406 of HY-116 and the 406 of HY-62.20 and HY-62.34 have `Vary: Accept`, because `Accept` decides them. <a id="HY-117.4"></a> Every other plain text response, the 500 of HY-43 and HY-66 of a representation request included, has no `Vary`, because it has `Cache-Control: no-store` (HY-65) and `Accept` does not decide it. <a id="HY-117.5"></a> A cache gives a stored response only to a request whose listed headers are equal (RFC 9110, section 12.5.5; RFC 9111, section 4.1), so a response never reaches a request that would have received another.

- **HY-118** <a id="HY-118.1"></a> A route may declare `representations`, an ordered list. <a id="HY-118.2"></a> Each entry has `type`, a media type; `parameters`, a map from each required parameter name of the type to the list of the values that the entry serves, such as `{"version": ["1"]}`, or an empty map; `methods`, a nonempty subset of `GET`, `POST`, `PUT` and `DELETE`; and `vary`, the request header names that its responses depend on besides `Accept`, such as `Authorization`, or an empty list. <a id="HY-118.3"></a> An entry with `GET` also answers `HEAD` with the headers of its `GET` response and no body (RFC 9110, section 9.3.2). <a id="HY-118.4"></a> The application provides one representation handler for each entry, by the route name and the type. <a id="HY-118.5"></a> The manifest check (HY-2) rejects, comparing without regard to case, a duplicate type in one route, a type equal to `text/html` or `application/vnd.hyper+json`, a type whose type or subtype is `*`, a parameter named `q`, a type, a parameter name or a value that is not valid (RFC 9110, section 8.3.1), an empty `methods`, an empty value list, a `vary` name that is not a field name (RFC 9110, section 5.1), a `vary` name `Accept` or `Cookie` and two equal `vary` names; opening the application fails for an entry without a handler and for a handler of a type that its route does not declare.

- **HY-119** <a id="HY-119.1"></a> A declared type matches an `Accept` range that names it with a served value for every required parameter and no other parameter before `q`. <a id="HY-119.2"></a> A quoted value equals the same unquoted value (RFC 9110, section 5.6.6). <a id="HY-119.3"></a> Among the matching ranges of a type the server takes the one with the highest weight, then the first in `Accept` order, and the handler receives its parameter values. <a id="HY-119.4"></a> The `Content-Type` of the response is the type followed, for each required parameter in the order of `parameters`, by `; <name>=<value>`, with the name in lowercase and the value unquoted when it is a token and quoted otherwise.

- **HY-120** <a id="HY-120.1"></a> The application opens the session of a request with the session store that its host passes to it (HY-97, HY-100), only for `<base path>/_hyper/keep` (HY-40) and for a request that selects `text/html` or `application/vnd.hyper+json` (HY-116). <a id="HY-120.2"></a> It opens it after the checks of HY-116, HY-62 (its 405, 406 and shell), HY-127, HY-59.7 and HY-114 that apply to the request, and before the token check of HY-24 and the first handler, because the token check is the first step that reads the session. <a id="HY-120.3"></a> A request that one of those checks refuses opens no session and waits for no lock of HY-104. <a id="HY-120.4"></a> A representation request therefore opens no session, holds no lock of HY-104 and sets no session cookie.

- **HY-121** <a id="HY-121.1"></a> A representation request runs its handler and no context handler, loader, action or shared handler; the handler reads the selection value of HY-62 from its request, as a loader does. <a id="HY-121.2"></a> The server reads no session and no cookie, sets no cookie and sends no `csrf`, and the request that the handler receives has no `Cookie` header, so the response depends only on the request line, the headers other than `Cookie`, the body and the stored data that the handler reads. <a id="HY-121.3"></a> A request that writes with a session is an action (HY-24). <a id="HY-121.4"></a> The method check of HY-116 comes before the 415 and the 400 of this rule. <a id="HY-121.5"></a> A `HEAD` request of an entry with `GET` runs the handler with the request method `GET`; `App.handle` returns that `GET` response with its body, which the response hook (HY-60), the response limit (HY-66) and `around` (HY-97) receive, and the host writes its status and its headers, with the `Content-Length` of that body, and no body. <a id="HY-121.6"></a> A method that `methods` does not list, other than `HEAD` for an entry with `GET`, receives 405 with `Allow`, which lists the methods that the entry answers in the order `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, separated by `, `. <a id="HY-121.7"></a> A `GET`, `HEAD` or `DELETE` whose body has a size (HY-59.5) other than 0 receives 400 with the text `Bad Request`, because these methods carry no body that the handler reads. <a id="HY-121.8"></a> A `POST` or `PUT` without `Content-Type`, or whose `Content-Type` media type, compared without regard to case and without its parameters, is not `application/json`, receives 415; the body limit of HY-59 applies, and a body that is not valid UTF-8, or that is not the JSON text of a value of the data model as HY-54 decodes kept values (an integer literal is an integer and other number literals are floats; a number outside ±(2^53 − 1) or not finite, 512 nested containers, a lone surrogate escape and a key that starts with U+0000 fail), receives 400 with the text `Bad Request`. <a id="HY-121.9"></a> The handler reads the decoded value with `json()` of its request (PHP `Request::json()`, Node and Python `request.json()`).

- **HY-122** <a id="HY-122.1"></a> A representation handler returns a response with a status, a body, and headers; the body is a value of the data model other than null, or null, which means that the response has no body. <a id="HY-122.2"></a> The status is one of 200, 201, 204, 400, 401, 403, 404, 406, 409, 412, 415, 422 and 428; a 401 requires `WWW-Authenticate`, a 201 requires `Location`, and a 204 with a body and a 200 without a body fail with HY-43. <a id="HY-122.3"></a> A response without a body has no `Content-Type`. <a id="HY-122.4"></a> The handler may set only `Location`, `WWW-Authenticate` and `Cache-Control` (HY-130). <a id="HY-122.5"></a> A `Location` that is an application path (HY-46) gets the base path of the request, the data base path under a chosen request (HY-62.19), as every `Location` of the application does (HY-8); a `Location` that is an absolute URI (RFC 3986, section 4.3) is sent as it is; another value, such as `//host/path` or `posts/8`, fails with HY-43. <a id="HY-122.6"></a> A response without a `Cache-Control` from the handler has `Cache-Control: no-cache`, or `private, no-cache` for a request with `Authorization`; for such a request, a handler value without the directive `private` or `no-store`, or with `public` or `s-maxage`, fails with HY-43, as HY-52 requires of a page (RFC 9111, section 3.5); directive names compare without regard to case (RFC 9111, section 5.2). <a id="HY-122.7"></a> A response with a status of 400 or more has `Cache-Control: no-store` (HY-65), and a handler that sets `Cache-Control` on it fails with HY-43. <a id="HY-122.8"></a> Another header or status fails with HY-43. <a id="HY-122.9"></a> The server writes the body as the JSON text of HY-54 with the `Content-Type` of HY-119. <a id="HY-122.10"></a> A response with status 200 to a `GET` or `HEAD` has the strong `ETag` `"<digits>"` of the first 32 hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 digest of the `Content-Type`, a line feed and the body; a `GET` or `HEAD` whose `If-None-Match` equals it receives 304 with the headers of the 200 response except `Content-Type` and no body, as HY-53 states, and the tag is strong, unlike that of HY-53, because no token varies its bytes; a response with another status has no `ETag`, and an `If-None-Match` does not change it. <a id="HY-122.11"></a> The server gives the handler the function `etag(body)`, which returns that tag for a body of the selected type, so that a `PUT` or `DELETE` handler compares `If-Match` with it (RFC 9110, section 13.1.1). <a id="HY-122.12"></a> The response hook (HY-60, with a new empty reply), the frame policy (HY-45), the response limit (HY-66), the errors of the ORM (HY-107: `NO_ROWS` is 404 with the text `Not Found`, and `REVISION_CHANGED` is 412 with the text `Precondition Failed`, both plain text with `Cache-Control: no-store`) and the errors of HY-43 apply as to a page; HY-52, HY-53 for its weak tag and HY-103 do not, because the handler has no reply.

## JSON response

- **HY-17** <a id="HY-17.1"></a> A JSON response has this shape. <a id="HY-17.2"></a> Keys keep their order. <a id="HY-17.3"></a> Every server writes the JSON text of a response, and decodes the kept values of HY-38 and HY-40, as HY-54 states.

```json
{
  "env": { "timezone": "+09:00" },
  "route": "board.show",
  "params": { "id": "7" },
  "build": "<build id>",
  "context": { "hash": "<context hash>", "value": { "name": "Board" } },
  "shared": { "title": "Post", "csrf": "token" },
  "regions": {
    "content": { "post": { "id": 7 } },
    "reader": { "large": false },
    "left": { "count": 3 }
  },
  "kept": {
    "reader": { "large": true }
  }
}
```

`build` is the build id (HY-125); `context` is present only for an application with a context and holds `value` only as HY-128 states. `regions` holds the loader data. `kept` holds, by region and path, the `server` and `cookie` kept values that the server read for the regions in `regions` and that conform to the region data (HY-38). A region without such values has no entry.

- **HY-18** <a id="HY-18.1"></a> For a document request, `regions` contains every region in manifest order, without absent route regions (HY-75). <a id="HY-18.2"></a> For a region request, it contains the page region first, then every other region that uses a changed topic, in manifest order.

- **HY-19** <a id="HY-19.1"></a> The changed topics of a request are the topics recorded by the previous action (HY-25) and `path` (HY-11).

## Application context

An application sends with every JSON response values that change only with its configuration and its build, such as messages, asset URLs and names. The context holds them: a part of the shared data that the browser holds by its hash, and that a JSON response holds only when it changed.

- **HY-124** <a id="HY-124.1"></a> An application may declare a context handler. <a id="HY-124.2"></a> The server calls it once for every request that selects `text/html` or `application/vnd.hyper+json` (HY-116) and that reaches the shared handler, which is a request without an action, a request whose action returns the route page (HY-26, HY-58) and a request whose action lets `REVISION_CHANGED` escape, which the server answers as the page with status 409 (HY-107), after the action of the request and before the shared handler and any loader, so that the context holds what the action wrote, with the value of the selection of HY-62 (null for an application without client rendering), and the handler returns a map of the data model (HY-44), the context. <a id="HY-124.3"></a> A loader or the shared handler that then stops or fails the request does not undo the call. <a id="HY-124.4"></a> A request whose action redirects (HY-25, HY-50), stops (HY-51, HY-58) or fails with HY-43, and a request that hyper answers before any handler runs, cause no call. <a id="HY-124.5"></a> The handler reads no value of the request: no path, no parameter, no query, no header, no session and no cookie. <a id="HY-124.6"></a> The context therefore depends only on the selection value, the build and the stored data that the handler reads, and its hash (HY-125) identifies it. <a id="HY-124.7"></a> The context is the member `context` of the shared data (HY-10); templates read it as `context.<name>`. <a id="HY-124.8"></a> A shared handler that returns the key `context` fails with HY-43. <a id="HY-124.9"></a> An application without the declaration has no member `context`. <a id="HY-124.10"></a> In Node the context is a `Map` (HY-54), because a plain object orders its integer-like keys first and would give another JSON text than PHP and Python; a Node context handler may return a promise of it, which the server awaits, and another value fails with HY-43.

- **HY-125** <a id="HY-125.1"></a> The build id is the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the outputs that the browser runs: the client entry, its chunks, `manifest.json` and the template files and the index of the asset build (HYC-16), without the static shell of HY-62, which holds the id. <a id="HY-125.2"></a> The path of an output is, for a file below `public/assets` (the entry, its chunks and the template files), its URL path without the leading slash, such as `assets/hyper-<hash>.js`, and, for `manifest.json` and `templates.index.json`, its name in the directory of `--output`. <a id="HY-125.3"></a> The build hashes the outputs in the order of their paths, compared as bytes, each path as UTF-8 followed by a NUL byte, the length of its file as 8 bytes big-endian and the bytes of the file. <a id="HY-125.4"></a> It writes the id as `{"build":"<build id>"}` into `build.json` of the asset output, which the hash excludes, and of the program directory (HY-48), and every server reads the id when the application opens; `open` fails with the absolute path of a `build.json` that is missing or that does not hold exactly the key `build` with a build id of 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. <a id="HY-125.5"></a> The server build (HY-48) takes the path of the `build.json` of the asset output with its option `--build` and writes the same file into the program directory; it fails with the path when the file is missing or does not hold a build id of 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. <a id="HY-125.7"></a> A document has the `html` definition `build`, the text `<meta name="hyper-build" content="<build id>">`, which the layout renders with `{# build}` once inside `<head>` (HY-3, HY-12); the build fails for a layout that does not place `{# build}` exactly once, as for `{# title}` and `{# data}` (HY-48); the check counts the placement and does not check that it lies inside `<head>`. <a id="HY-125.8"></a> The static shell has the same element. <a id="HY-125.9"></a> The server checks the context by HY-44 for every request that calls the context handler. <a id="HY-125.10"></a> For a JSON response and for a document that embeds its data (HY-31), and for no other response, it then writes the JSON text of HY-54 of the context once and computes the context hash from it; that text is the text of the member `value` of HY-128 and the text of the hash below. <a id="HY-125.11"></a> A document that does not embed its data holds neither the hash nor `value`, so the server renders it from the context map and does not write that text. <a id="HY-125.12"></a> The context hash is the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the bytes `{"build":"<build id>","context":`, then that text, then `}`, which is the JSON text of HY-54 of that map, so every server computes the same hash for the same context, and a new build gives a new hash.

- **HY-126** <a id="HY-126.1"></a> The read paths of HY-73 do not apply to `context`: the server sends it whole, because one context serves every route and its hash covers all of it. <a id="HY-126.2"></a> HY-71 applies to it as to all shared data.

- **HY-127** <a id="HY-127.1"></a> A region request and a document request may send the header `Hyper-Context` with the context hash that the browser holds. <a id="HY-127.2"></a> An application with a context checks the header of every request that selects `text/html` or `application/vnd.hyper+json` and that HY-62 does not answer with its 405, 406 or shell, right after the method check of HY-116 and before HY-59.7 and HY-59.8, the file limit of HY-114, the token check of HY-24, the context handler and any loader or action: a value that is not 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters makes the server respond with status 400 and the text `Bad Request` (HY-58). <a id="HY-127.3"></a> An application without a context does not read the header. <a id="HY-127.4"></a> An HTML request with a valid value is answered as without it, because a document holds the whole context.

- **HY-128** <a id="HY-128.1"></a> Every JSON response (HY-17) holds, after `params`, the member `build`, the build id. <a id="HY-128.2"></a> A JSON response of an application with a context holds after it the member `context`: `{"hash": <context hash>}`, followed by `"value": <context>` when the request has no `Hyper-Context` or names another hash. <a id="HY-128.3"></a> The member `context` of `shared` is absent from a JSON response; before it renders, the browser code inserts the context into `shared` at its position of HY-10: the `value` of the response when it has one, and otherwise the held context. <a id="HY-128.4"></a> The Node server renders its documents with that same code (HY-54) from the context map, and puts the member `context` with `hash` and `value` into the value that it renders only for a document that embeds its data. <a id="HY-128.5"></a> A document that embeds its data (HY-31) embeds `build` and `context` with `value`.

## Browser

- **HYC-1** <a id="HYC-1.1"></a> The browser code routes the response URL path (after removing the base path) with the manifest routes. <a id="HYC-1.2"></a> The route name must equal `route` in the response; otherwise rendering fails. <a id="HYC-1.3"></a> The page region template is the template of that route. <a id="HYC-1.4"></a> The browser code routes a request path by HY-4 to HY-8 and HY-49.

- **HYC-2** <a id="HYC-2.1"></a> The htmx extension requests JSON (`Accept: application/vnd.hyper+json`) only when the `id` of the request target element is the name of the page region. <a id="HYC-2.2"></a> It converts a JSON region response into this HTML and gives it to htmx in place of the response text: `<title>` with the title rendered alone, then the page region rendered alone, then `<hx-partial hx-target="#<name>" hx-swap="innerMorph">` with each other region rendered alone. <a id="HYC-2.3"></a> Before htmx swaps, the browser applies the stylesheet links of the layout of the response (HYC-15). <a id="HYC-2.4"></a> htmx then performs the swap, the title change and the history update. <a id="HYC-2.5"></a> A response whose content type is not `application/vnd.hyper+json` passes unchanged.

- **HYC-8** <a id="HYC-8.1"></a> In client-side rendering, a static shell declares the base path of the server with `<meta name="hyper-api" content="/api">`. <a id="HYC-8.2"></a> The browser code requests the document JSON for the current path while it loads the templates of the route (HYC-12), routes the response URL after redirects (HYC-1), renders the document (HY-12), applies the stylesheet links of its head (HYC-15), replaces the attributes of the `html` element (HYC-6), the title and the body with the rendered ones, and lets htmx process the new body. <a id="HYC-8.3"></a> A current path that matches no route renders the body text `Not Found`.

- **HYC-3** <a id="HYC-3.1"></a> In client-side rendering, the extension prefixes the same-origin request path of every region request with the base path, removes the base path from history paths, and replaces htmx history restoration with HYC-8 for the restored path. <a id="HYC-3.2"></a> A later restoration cancels an earlier one that is still loading, and only the latest one is rendered; HYC-23 orders restorations with region requests.

- **HYC-15** <a id="HYC-15.1"></a> The stylesheet links of a head are its `link` elements that have an `href` attribute and whose `rel` attribute contains the token `stylesheet`, compared without regard to ASCII case. <a id="HYC-15.2"></a> The key of a link is the value of its `href` attribute resolved against the URL of the page. <a id="HYC-15.3"></a> When the browser shows new content, it applies the stylesheet links of the head of a source document to the head of the page:

  - <a id="HYC-15.4"></a> client-side rendering of a document (HYC-8, HYC-3): the rendered document;
  - <a id="HYC-15.5"></a> a JSON region response (HYC-2): the layout rendered with the shared data of the response, with the context of HY-128 as its member `context`, as root data, the title rendered alone as the definition `title`, the definition `build` of the build of the page (HYC-22), and an empty definition `data` and an empty definition for every manifest region;
  - <a id="HYC-15.6"></a> the HTML document that htmx requests to restore a page from history in server-side rendering (HYC-4): that document.

  <a id="HYC-15.7"></a> The browser applies the links in three steps:

  1. <a id="HYC-15.8"></a> It walks the stylesheet links of the source in order; a key that appears again counts only at its first link. <a id="HYC-15.9"></a> For each link it keeps the first stylesheet link of the page with the same key that stands after the last kept link, and otherwise inserts a copy of the source link after the last kept or inserted link, or, before the first kept link, in front of the first stylesheet link of the page, or at the end of the head when the page has none.
  2. <a id="HYC-15.10"></a> It waits until every inserted link, and every kept link that an earlier application inserted and that is still loading, has loaded. <a id="HYC-15.11"></a> Only then does it show the content.
  3. <a id="HYC-15.12"></a> After it shows the content, it removes every other stylesheet link of the page, so that the stylesheet links of the page are those of the source in their order.

  <a id="HYC-15.13"></a> Other elements of the head, such as `style` elements, stay. <a id="HYC-15.14"></a> When a later application starts before an earlier one shows its content, only the later one removes links. <a id="HYC-15.15"></a> When a link fails to load, the browser removes the links that it inserted for this application, does not show the content and reports the failure as HYC-14 defines. <a id="HYC-15.16"></a> The first document of server-side rendering already has its stylesheet links and needs no application.

- **HYC-22** <a id="HYC-22.1"></a> The build of the page is the `hyper-build` of its document (HY-125), and the browser renders the definition `build` with it. <a id="HYC-22.2"></a> The browser holds the context and its hash: from the embedded data, or from the first JSON response, whose request has no `Hyper-Context`. <a id="HYC-22.3"></a> A document without `#hy-data` holds no context, so its next JSON request has no `Hyper-Context`. <a id="HYC-22.4"></a> The browser sends the held hash with every region request and document request (HY-127). <a id="HYC-22.5"></a> A response with `value` replaces the held context before the browser renders. <a id="HYC-22.6"></a> A response whose `build` differs from the build of the page makes the browser load the page URL of the response (HYC-1, without the data base path of HY-62) as a new document with `GET` instead of rendering, because the page runs the client code of another build. <a id="HYC-22.7"></a> When htmx restores a page from history by requesting its HTML (HYC-4), a document whose `hyper-build` differs from the build of the page is loaded as a new document instead of being swapped. <a id="HYC-22.8"></a> A response without `value` whose `hash` differs from the held hash is an error of the request (HYC-14).

- **HYC-23** <a id="HYC-23.1"></a> The browser renders only the response of its latest region request; the response of an earlier one is not rendered, as a later restoration cancels an earlier one (HYC-3). <a id="HYC-23.2"></a> A restoration (HYC-3, HYC-8) counts as a region request for this rule; a document request of HYC-7 does not, because HYC-7 drops its own response when another response replaced the held data. <a id="HYC-23.3"></a> A response that is not rendered is not a failure (HYC-14).

- **HYC-24** <a id="HYC-24.1"></a> `HyperOptions` of the browser code takes `functions`, a map from names to functions, and registers them in the template engine (template FUN-43). <a id="HYC-24.2"></a> The `App` of every server takes the same map as its option `functions` (HY-106) when the application opens, and the Node server registers it through `createApplication` of the browser code, so the server and the browser register the same names (template FUN-47); a registration that fails (template FUN-44) fails the open. <a id="HYC-24.5"></a> An entry that is not a function fails the open with the argument error of template RT-5. <a id="HYC-24.6"></a> A render that calls a name that is neither built in nor registered fails with HY-43.

## Client rendering on the server

- **HY-62** <a id="HY-62.1"></a> An application may declare client rendering, so that one server answers the client-rendered pages and the server-rendered pages of one manifest with the same handlers. <a id="HY-62.2"></a> The declaration has a static shell, a data base path and a selection:

  - <a id="HY-62.3"></a> The shell is the absolute path of an HTML file that contains `<meta name="hyper-api" content="<data base path>">` (HYC-8). <a id="HY-62.4"></a> The server reads it when the application opens.
  - <a id="HY-62.5"></a> The data base path follows HY-8 and is not empty. <a id="HY-62.6"></a> No route path is the data base path or starts with it followed by `/`.
  - <a id="HY-62.7"></a> The selection receives every request and returns a choice: whether the request is of a client-rendered page, chosen for example by the `Host` header, and a value, such as the stored service of the host. <a id="HY-62.8"></a> In PHP the choice is `new Choice(chosen: <bool>, value: <value>)`; in Node it is an object `{ chosen, value }` whose `chosen` is `true` or `false` and whose `value` is not `undefined`. <a id="HY-62.9"></a> The server calls the selection once per request, after HY-59.4 and HY-42 and before routing, with the request without its `Cookie` header: the choice decides the shell response and the path of a representation, and neither varies by `Cookie` (HY-117). <a id="HY-62.10"></a> In the Node server the selection may also return a promise of the choice, which the server awaits, because a selection that reads stored data reads it asynchronously in Node. <a id="HY-62.11"></a> A selection that throws, returns another value or returns a promise that rejects or resolves to another value fails with HY-43.
  - <a id="HY-62.12"></a> Every loader and action of the request reads the value of the choice from its request, `$request->selection()` in PHP and `request.selection()` in Node and Python, whether the selection chose the request or not. <a id="HY-62.13"></a> An application therefore reads the stored data that its selection and its handlers both need once per request and passes it as a value, without a cache. <a id="HY-62.14"></a> A request of an application without the declaration has the value null.

  <a id="HY-62.15"></a> The application fails to open when the shell file cannot be read, the shell does not declare the data base path, the data base path is empty or does not follow HY-8, or a route path lies under the data base path. <a id="HY-62.16"></a> A request that the selection does not choose is answered as without the declaration, with the base path of the application (HY-8). <a id="HY-62.17"></a> A chosen request is answered with the data base path in place of the base path of the application:

  1. <a id="HY-62.18"></a> `<data base path>/_hyper/keep` follows HY-40.
  2. <a id="HY-62.19"></a> A request path that starts with the data base path followed by `/` or the end of the path is routed after the data base path is removed, and `Location` headers include the data base path (HY-8). <a id="HY-62.20"></a> After the selection and the method check of HY-116, a request that selects a representation is answered by HY-121, and a request that selects `text/html` receives status 406 with the text `Not Acceptable` and `Vary: Accept`. <a id="HY-62.21"></a> Every other request is answered by HY-15 to HY-40 and HY-42 to HY-59: a document request and a region request receive JSON, and an action runs.
  3. <a id="HY-62.22"></a> Any other request path is routed as it is. <a id="HY-62.23"></a> A path without a route receives 404 and a method other than `GET` receives 405 (HY-27). <a id="HY-62.34"></a> Then a request that selects `application/vnd.hyper+json` or a representation (HY-116) receives status 406 with the text `Not Acceptable` and `Vary: Accept`, and a request that selects `text/html` receives status 200 with the bytes of the shell as its body and the response of the application to it has the headers `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8`, `Cache-Control: no-cache`, the `Vary` of HY-117 and the frame policy of HY-45, and no other header; its host may add headers as HY-130 allows. <a id="HY-62.25"></a> The shell holds the element `hyper-build` of HY-125, which the asset build writes.

  <a id="HY-62.26"></a> The 405 and 406 responses and the shell response of a chosen request run no loader or action, read no session (HY-45), and contain no request data. <a id="HY-62.27"></a> Every response of a chosen request carries the frame policy of HY-45 and is reported to the response hook of HY-60.

- **HYC-6** <a id="HYC-6.1"></a> When client-side rendering mounts a rendered document (HYC-8, HYC-3), the browser replaces the attributes of the `html` element with the attributes of the `html` element of the rendered document, in their order: an attribute that the rendered element does not have is removed. <a id="HYC-6.2"></a> A layout that renders `<html lang="{= language}">` therefore gives a client-rendered page the language of its data, as the server-rendered document has it. <a id="HYC-6.3"></a> The static shell that `scripts/build-assets.mjs` writes has no `lang` attribute, because it holds no data.

## Actions

- **HY-24** <a id="HY-24.1"></a> The session token is 32 random bytes that the server creates when the session first needs it. <a id="HY-24.2"></a> The value `csrf` of a response (HY-10) masks it: 32 random bytes `r` that the server draws once per response, followed by `r` XOR the token, written as 128 lowercase hexadecimal digits. <a id="HY-24.3"></a> Every response draws a new `r`, so no response contains the bytes of the token, and the compressed size of a response that also contains request input does not reveal it. <a id="HY-24.4"></a> An action request and a save of a kept value (HY-40) must contain the form field `_csrf` with a masked value of the session token: 128 lowercase hexadecimal digits whose second half XOR its first half equals the token, compared in constant time. <a id="HY-24.5"></a> Otherwise the server responds with status 403 and runs no action. <a id="HY-24.6"></a> The server never sends the token itself. <a id="HY-24.9"></a> A server holds the token as 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, and a session that holds another value in the place of the token gets a new token, as a session that holds none (HY-24.1), so that no masked value of the other value is valid; masking or verifying with a token or a mask in any other form fails with HY-43, while a form value that is not 128 lowercase hexadecimal digits is not valid (HY-24.5).

- **HY-72** <a id="HY-72.1"></a> An action renews the session with `renewSession()` of its reply when the visitor that the session belongs to changes, such as at sign-in and sign-out. <a id="HY-72.2"></a> After the action returns, the server moves the session values to a new session identifier, deletes the old session, creates a new session token and sets the new session cookie; the flash values of a redirect and the kept values stay. <a id="HY-72.3"></a> A page that the action renders carries a masked value of the new token. <a id="HY-72.4"></a> A loader or the shared handler that calls `renewSession()` fails with HY-43, because the page that it renders carries the old token.

- **HY-25** <a id="HY-25.1"></a> An action that succeeds returns a redirect. <a id="HY-25.2"></a> The server responds with status 303 and `Location`, stores the flash values and the changed topics in the session, and removes them after the next request reads them. <a id="HY-25.3"></a> The browser follows the redirect with the same headers, and htmx records the final URL in history. <a id="HY-25.4"></a> The flash values of a result are values of the data model (HY-44): storing a value outside it fails when it is stored, with the error of the data model. <a id="HY-25.5"></a> A flash value stored again under its name replaces the value at the place of that name, and a changed topic recorded again keeps its first place. <a id="HY-25.6"></a> A flash name and a changed topic are strings: another value fails with `TypeError` and the message `a flash name is not a string (HY-25)` or `a changed topic is not a string (HY-25)` in the three servers, also for a PHP caller without strict types.

- **HY-26** <a id="HY-26.1"></a> An action that rejects its input returns invalid data. <a id="HY-26.2"></a> The server responds with status 422 and renders the route page with the route data merged with the invalid data, as JSON for a JSON request and as a document otherwise.

## Data

- **HYC-10** <a id="HYC-10.1"></a> The output of a region is a function of its template, the shared data and the region data. <a id="HYC-10.2"></a> The browser changes the page only by replacing region data and rendering it. <a id="HYC-10.3"></a> Form controls hold the values that a user is entering; every other screen state, such as a sort order or an open panel, is region data.

- **HY-30** <a id="HY-30.1"></a> A route may declare route regions, for example `"regions": [{ "name": "rows", "template": "board/rows.tpl" }]`. <a id="HY-30.2"></a> A part of a page that changes in the browser without a request to the application is a route region; the browser may load the template files that the change renders and that it has not loaded (HYC-12). <a id="HY-30.3"></a> The route template, or a template that it includes or places by path, places each route region with `{# name}`, without block arguments, inside an element whose `id` is the region name; `make templates-check` fails when no template of that graph places a route region. <a id="HY-30.4"></a> A route region loader may return `null`, which makes the region absent from that response (HY-75). <a id="HY-30.5"></a> Region names are unique across the manifest regions and every route region. <a id="HY-30.6"></a> Each route region has its own loader. <a id="HY-30.7"></a> The page region receives every route region as HTML (HY-13), and every JSON response that contains the page region contains the route regions right after it.

- **HY-75** <a id="HY-75.1"></a> A route region is present in a response when its loader returns data, and absent when it returns `null`. <a id="HY-75.2"></a> An absent route region has no entry in `regions` of the JSON response, in the embedded data (HY-31) or in `kept`, and the page region receives no definition for it, so `{?# name}` is false; a template that places a route region that may be absent places its element inside `{?# name}…{/}`. <a id="HY-75.3"></a> A response carries no kept value of an absent region. <a id="HY-75.4"></a> The browser holds only the present route regions (HYC-4), so `data`, `render`, `set` and `hy-set` fail for an absent one (HYC-11). <a id="HY-75.5"></a> After it renders or swaps the page region, the browser checks that every present route region of the held route has exactly one element with its `id` in the page and that no absent route region has one; otherwise it sets `hy-error="0"` on the body (HYC-14). <a id="HY-75.6"></a> This lets a page that places views at request time under one route, such as a page that an administrator composes, declare a route region for a view that only some of its pages place.

- **HY-31** <a id="HY-31.1"></a> The layout places `{# data}` once, before `</body>`. <a id="HY-31.2"></a> The embedded data is the part of the document JSON value (HY-17) that the browser can change: `env`, `route`, `params`, `build`, `context` with `value` (HY-128) and `shared` as the JSON response has them (HY-73), `regions` with only the route regions of the route (HY-30) in their order, and `kept` with only the entries of those regions. <a id="HY-31.3"></a> A document embeds its data when the reply of its request asks for it (HY-92) and a route region of the route is present (HY-75): the definition `data` then renders the reserved template `hyper/data.tpl`, whose source is exactly `<script type="application/json" id="hy-data">{= json(response) | raw}</script>`, with `response` equal to the embedded data. <a id="HY-31.4"></a> Otherwise the definition `data` is empty and the document has no `#hy-data`, so its source holds only the HTML of the page. <a id="HY-31.5"></a> A document of client-side rendering (HYC-8) never embeds its data, because the browser holds the data of the JSON response that it rendered. <a id="HY-31.6"></a> The PHP server and the Node server compute and render the embedded data the same way, so a document keeps the same bytes on both. <a id="HY-31.7"></a> A region request does not render it. <a id="HY-31.8"></a> A JSON response keeps every region (HY-18), because the browser renders them.

- **HY-92** <a id="HY-92.1"></a> A loader, an action or the shared handler of a request makes the HTML document of its response embed its data (HY-31) with `embedData()` of its reply (HY-52): `$reply->embedData()` in PHP, `reply.embedData()` in Node and `reply.embed_data()` in Python. <a id="HY-92.2"></a> Without the call a document embeds no data. <a id="HY-92.3"></a> The call changes no JSON response (HY-17), redirect or stop, and a request of client-side rendering (HY-62) receives the shell or JSON, which hold no embedded data. <a id="HY-92.4"></a> An application decides it per request, for example by the stored service of the host that its selection reads (HY-62).

- **HY-71** <a id="HY-71.1"></a> The data that the server sends is public to the visitor of the request. <a id="HY-71.2"></a> Shared data, region data and kept values reach the browser in the embedded data (HY-31), in every JSON response (HY-17) and in client-side rendering (HYC-8), so a value passed to a template does not stay on the server. <a id="HY-71.3"></a> A loader and the shared handler return only values that the visitor of the request may see: a value that the page does not show, such as a password hash, a session token or personal data that the visitor may not see, is never part of them. <a id="HY-71.4"></a> The server also removes every value that the templates do not read (HY-73), but that removal does not make a value safe to return. <a id="HY-71.5"></a> A value that the page shows reaches the browser in the HTML anyway. <a id="HY-71.6"></a> The masked CSRF token is shared data (HY-10, HY-24), because the browser sends it back with every form; the session token itself is never sent.

- **HY-73** <a id="HY-73.1"></a> The server sends only the data that the templates of a route read, except `context`, which it sends whole (HY-126). <a id="HY-73.2"></a> The read paths are computed from the template ASTs before any request, and they include at least every value that rendering reads, so rendering the kept data gives the same bytes as rendering the loader data.

  - <a id="HY-73.3"></a> A path is a list of steps from the root data: a map key, a list index written in decimal, or `*`, which stands for every entry of a map or every element of a list. <a id="HY-73.4"></a> A path read whole keeps its value as it is; a path read in part keeps only the paths below it that are read.
  - <a id="HY-73.5"></a> An expression has a set of paths. <a id="HY-73.6"></a> A variable has the root path of its name, together with the paths that a local variable of that name holds; a local variable holds the union of the paths of every assignment `{:x = e}` of its scope. <a id="HY-73.7"></a> The loop variable of `{@ v = e}` exists only in the body of that loop: there `v` has every path of `e` followed by `*` and the paths of the assignments to `v`, and neither its root path nor the paths of an outer loop variable of the same name. <a id="HY-73.8"></a> Outside the body the loop variable adds no path to `v`, so an assignment before the loop that reads the name of its loop variable, as in `{:p = page.x}{@ page = p.items}`, keeps the paths that it had before the loop. <a id="HY-73.9"></a> `v.value_` has the paths of `v`, and another loop meta field has none. <a id="HY-73.10"></a> A member, and an index whose key is a string or number literal, add the key to every path. <a id="HY-73.11"></a> Another index reads its object and its key whole and has no path. <a id="HY-73.12"></a> `a ?? b` has the paths of `a` and `b`, a ternary the paths of its two results, and every other expression none.
  - <a id="HY-73.13"></a> An expression reads its paths whole when its value is output, is the test of `{? }`, `{:? }` or a ternary, is an operand of an operator other than `??`, is an argument of a function, a member call or a class call, the object of a member call, an item, key, value or spread of a list or map literal, or the key of an index. <a id="HY-73.14"></a> A loop `{@ v = e}` reads every path of `e` followed by `*` in part, so the loop keeps every entry.
  - <a id="HY-73.15"></a> An include `{+ path}` reads in the scope of the including template. <a id="HY-73.16"></a> A block with a path reads its template in a new scope, where the root names hold their root paths and every scope argument holds the paths of its expression in the calling scope; a block that places a template already being placed above it reads nothing, because rendering fails there (RT-22 of the template language). <a id="HY-73.17"></a> A block that places a definition reads nothing.
  - <a id="HY-73.18"></a> The read paths of the shared data of a route are those of the layout, the title, every manifest region template, the route template and every route region template, and `csrf` whole when a route region keeps a value on the server (HYC-13). <a id="HY-73.19"></a> The read paths of the data of a region are those of its template, the route template for the page region, and the kept paths of a route region whole. <a id="HY-73.20"></a> `hyper/data.tpl` reads nothing.
  - <a id="HY-73.29"></a> Before it renders or encodes a page, the server keeps of the shared data and of every region's data only their read paths: a map keeps the keys that a path names, in their order in the data, with their values kept recursively, and every key under `*`; a list keeps its length, with each element kept under `*` and the paths of its index and with `null` at an index that no path names; any other value stays as it is. <a id="HY-73.22"></a> A map that becomes empty stays a map.
  - <a id="HY-73.23"></a> The build writes the read paths of every route to `reads.json` of the server program (HY-48), and the Node server computes them with the browser package when the application opens. <a id="HY-73.25"></a> `data(region)` (HYC-11) returns the kept data, so a path that no template reads is not there.

  <a id="HY-73.28"></a> The kept data renders the same bytes as the data.

## Browser data

- **HYC-4** <a id="HYC-4.1"></a> The browser holds the data of the last response that it rendered: the environment, the route, the parameters, the shared data and the data of the route regions of the route (HY-30). <a id="HYC-4.2"></a> When a server-rendered page opens with `open()` of the browser code, and when htmx restores a page from history by requesting its HTML, the browser reads the embedded data from the element `#hy-data` (HY-31), replaces all held data with it and starts loading the templates of the route (HYC-12). <a id="HYC-4.3"></a> A document without `#hy-data` leaves no held data, and the browser obtains the data with HYC-7 when it first needs it. <a id="HYC-4.4"></a> It needs the data when the page opens only when a `localStorage` or `sessionStorage` value is stored for a kept path of a route region of the route (HY-37, HY-38), so a page that is only viewed and has no such value sends no request beyond its document. <a id="HYC-4.5"></a> A region response (HYC-2) replaces all held data with its own, because it contains the shared data, the page region and every present route region (HY-17, HY-18, HY-30), which is all that the browser holds. <a id="HYC-4.6"></a> The browser also holds the context of the application and the build of the page (HYC-22). <a id="HYC-4.7"></a> `render` (HYC-11) replaces held region data.

- **HYC-7** <a id="HYC-7.1"></a> The browser obtains the data that it does not hold with one document request (HY-15) for the URL of the current page, its path and its query, with `Accept: application/vnd.hyper+json`. <a id="HYC-7.2"></a> It obtains the data when `data`, `render`, `set` or `hy-set` (HYC-11, HYC-5) names a route region of the route of the current page while it holds no data, and when the page opens with a stored browser kept value (HYC-4). <a id="HYC-7.3"></a> A call that names another region sends no request: `data` returns nothing, and the other calls fail. <a id="HYC-7.4"></a> Calls that need the data while the request is pending wait for the same request. <a id="HYC-7.5"></a> The response must be a JSON response with status 200 whose URL routes to the route of the current page (HYC-1). <a id="HYC-7.6"></a> The browser then applies the browser kept values (HY-38), holds the data and renders every present route region of the route from it as HY-38 renders the regions of an embedded document, so that the page shows the data that the browser holds, also when the data changed after the server rendered the HTML; the call then continues with the held data. <a id="HYC-7.7"></a> When a response (HYC-2, HYC-4) replaced the held data while the request was pending, the browser drops the response of the request, and the call continues with the held data. <a id="HYC-7.8"></a> Another response, a network failure or a response that cannot be decoded leaves no held data, marks the region of the call, or the body when the page opens, with the status of the response or `0` (HYC-14), and fails the call; the next call that needs the data sends the request again. <a id="HYC-7.9"></a> The request runs the loaders of the page again as its HTML request did, so a loader of a `GET` request changes no stored state (RFC 9110, section 9.2.1), and the page of an action that rendered in place (HY-26, HY-58, HY-69) receives the data of the `GET` request of its URL.

- **HYC-11** <a id="HYC-11.1"></a> The browser code provides `data(region)`, which returns a promise of the held data of a region; `render(region, data)`, which replaces the held data of a region; and `set(region, path, value)`, which replaces one value at a dotted path (map keys and list indexes) in the held data of a region. <a id="HYC-11.2"></a> The region is a route region of the held route (HY-30); another region fails. <a id="HYC-11.3"></a> A path that the data does not contain fails. <a id="HYC-11.4"></a> `render` and `set` then render the region alone (HY-13) and swap it into the region element with `innerMorph`. <a id="HYC-11.5"></a> The page region uses the template of the held route and the held route regions (HY-13). <a id="HYC-11.6"></a> These operations send no request, except the document request of HYC-7 while the browser holds no data. <a id="HYC-11.7"></a> There is no change tracking: the code that changes data asks for the rendering. <a id="HYC-11.8"></a> Calls run one after another in call order, and each starts from the held data that the previous call left. <a id="HYC-11.9"></a> A call checks the held data of its own region: when a response (HYC-4) replaced it before the swap, the call ends without swapping, holding or storing; when a response replaced it during the swap, the call does not hold or store and renders the region again from the held data. <a id="HYC-11.10"></a> A response that leaves the region unchanged does not affect the call.

- **HYC-5** <a id="HYC-5.1"></a> A template may give an element the attribute `hy-set="path=value; path=value"`, where each value is a JSON literal and each path follows HYC-11. <a id="HYC-5.2"></a> A click on the element, or on an element inside it, runs every assignment in the held data of the closest enclosing element whose `id` is the name of a route region of the held route, or of the route of the current page while the browser holds no data (HYC-7), and renders that region once. <a id="HYC-5.3"></a> The template computes the assigned values, for example `hy-set="service.close.flag={? service.close.flag}0{:}1{/}"`. <a id="HYC-5.4"></a> `hy-set` works only with JavaScript.

## Client stream subscription

- **HYC-17** <a id="HYC-17.1"></a> The TypeScript client `Hyper` of `packages/client` provides `subscribe(url, listener, options)`, which opens the event stream of `url` and returns a subscription with `close()`. <a id="HYC-17.2"></a> The request is made by the client's `options.fetch` (HyperOptions `fetch`; the global `fetch` when the option is absent) with method `GET`, the header `Accept: text/event-stream` and `credentials: 'same-origin'`, as the document requests of HYC-7 are made. <a id="HYC-17.3"></a> The listener has `onEvent(event)`, which receives each event with its `event`, `data` and `id` (HYC-18), and `onError(error)`, which receives each failure of HYC-20. <a id="HYC-17.4"></a> The options are `watchdogMs` (HYC-20). <a id="HYC-17.5"></a> `subscribe` throws when the client is disposed (HYC-21) and when `watchdogMs` is not a positive finite number. <a id="HYC-17.6"></a> This subscription is carried only by the TypeScript client; the PHP, Python and Node servers have no client, and no other client of this repository has a stream.

- **HYC-18** <a id="HYC-18.1"></a> The body of the response is read as a WHATWG HTML "server-sent events" event stream: the fields `data`, `event`, `id` and `retry`, the lines ended by CRLF, LF or CR, the lines that begin with `:` as comments, and an event dispatched at each blank line. <a id="HYC-18.2"></a> The `event` of an event is its `event` field, or `message` when it has none, and its `data` is the `data` fields of the event joined by LF. <a id="HYC-18.3"></a> The `id` of an event is the last event ID that the standard keeps: the value of the last `id` field that the stream sent, which an event without an `id` field also carries. <a id="HYC-18.4"></a> An `id` or `retry` field whose value is invalid, and a field with an unknown name, are ignored, as the standard says, and are not failures. <a id="HYC-18.5"></a> The implementation parses the stream with the npm package `eventsource-parser`, not with a hand-written parser: the line endings, the byte-order mark and the incomplete last line of the standard are what that maintained parser already implements (S1). <a id="HYC-18.6"></a> The package is the choice of this rule for the TypeScript client, and its exact version is pinned with its reason in `docs/operations/dependencies.md` when the implementation row of HYC-17 is done. <a id="HYC-18.7"></a> A body that is not valid UTF-8 is a parse failure: the implementation decodes the body with a fatal decoder, and the failure is an error of HYC-20.

- **HYC-19** <a id="HYC-19.1"></a> The subscription keeps the last event ID and the retry delay, as the standard does. <a id="HYC-19.2"></a> The last event ID is the `id` of the last event that had an `id` field, and it is kept across reconnections; the retry delay is the value of the last `retry` field, in milliseconds, and defaults to 1000 when the server sent none. <a id="HYC-19.3"></a> When the stream ends, fails with an error of HYC-20, or answers with a status other than 2xx, the client reports the failure to `onError` and then reconnects after the retry delay. <a id="HYC-19.4"></a> The reconnection request carries the header `Last-Event-ID` with the last event ID when it is not empty, and carries no other cursor: no query parameter or other header states the position of the stream. <a id="HYC-19.5"></a> The 1000 ms default bounds the reconnection rate of a client whose server states no delay. <a id="HYC-19.6"></a> The client reconnects until `close()` or `dispose()` (HYC-21).

- **HYC-20** <a id="HYC-20.1"></a> The subscription has a byte watchdog. <a id="HYC-20.2"></a> When no byte of the body arrives for `watchdogMs` milliseconds, the stream fails with an error whose cause names the URL and the time, and the client then reconnects (HYC-19). <a id="HYC-20.3"></a> The watchdog restarts with each byte, and counts bytes, not events, so a stream that sends bytes without a complete event does not fail. <a id="HYC-20.4"></a> The default of `watchdogMs` is 30000: a silent connection then fails before the 60 s idle timeout that common reverse proxies apply by default, which would close it without telling the client. <a id="HYC-20.5"></a> Every failure of a subscription is reported to `onError` with its cause: a watchdog timeout, a non-2xx response (with its status and URL), a network failure, and a parse failure of HYC-18. <a id="HYC-20.6"></a> No failure is dropped silently (P8). <a id="HYC-20.7"></a> A close or a dispose is not a failure and reports nothing.

- **HYC-21** <a id="HYC-21.1"></a> `dispose()` of the client aborts every subscription and every pending request. <a id="HYC-21.2"></a> For each subscription it aborts the request, clears the watchdog timer and the retry timer, and sets the subscription closed; it aborts every pending region request and document request of the client (HYC-3, HYC-7). <a id="HYC-21.3"></a> After `dispose()` returns, the client has no timer running and calls no listener, and a response that arrives later is discarded. <a id="HYC-21.4"></a> `dispose()` may be called more than once; a call after the first has no effect. <a id="HYC-21.5"></a> A `subscribe` after `dispose()` throws, so that no subscription starts after the client is disposed.

## Template delivery

- **HYC-12** <a id="HYC-12.1"></a> The browser loads a template when rendering reaches it. <a id="HYC-12.2"></a> It renders, and when the rendering requested templates that are not loaded, it loads each of them by its index URL and renders again, until the rendering completes or fails for another reason. <a id="HYC-12.3"></a> A template that no rendering reaches, such as the template of a branch that the data does not select, is not loaded, so a route whose template selects one of many views loads only the views that it shows. <a id="HYC-12.4"></a> The entry templates of a route are the layout, the title, every non-page region template, the route template and every route region template; for a region request the browser starts loading them with the request, at the same time, and when the response URL routes to another route, such as after a redirect, it loads the entry templates of that route. <a id="HYC-12.5"></a> When a server-rendered page opens, the browser loads no template; it loads the templates that it needs when it first renders a region of that page. <a id="HYC-12.6"></a> The browser never renders `hyper/data.tpl`, because a client-rendered document embeds no data (HY-31); the Node server, which renders it, checks that the index holds it. <a id="HYC-12.7"></a> A name that the index does not hold fails the rendering (HYC-14). <a id="HYC-12.8"></a> Loaded templates stay loaded until the page unloads. <a id="HYC-12.9"></a> The Node server, which renders every page, reads every template of the index when it opens.

- **HYC-16** <a id="HYC-16.1"></a> A page requests only the resources that it uses, and each resource at most once while the page is loaded. <a id="HYC-16.2"></a> A resource is a template file, a stylesheet or a script file. <a id="HYC-16.3"></a> The browser loads a template when rendering reaches it (HYC-12). <a id="HYC-16.4"></a> The layout links only the stylesheets of the content that it renders, and the browser applies the stylesheet links of each rendered head and keeps a link that is already applied (HYC-15); a stylesheet that the application links on every page is one that every page uses. <a id="HYC-16.5"></a> The asset build writes the client entry `public/assets/hyper-<hash>.js` and, for code that the entry imports with `import()` and does not import statically, chunk files `public/assets/hyper-chunk-<hash>.js`; the browser loads a chunk when that code first runs, by an absolute URL below `/assets/`, so the entry that the static shell inlines loads it too, and the browser loads a module once. <a id="HYC-16.6"></a> The asset build writes no file that the application names: it writes the template files and the index (HR-34), the entry, its chunks, `manifest.json` in the directory of `--output` with the URL of the entry as its only member `hyper`, and the static shell. <a id="HYC-16.7"></a> The application places and links its own stylesheets and names with `--static` the files below `public/` that the static deployment holds at the same path, such as the stylesheets that its layouts link; the asset build adds no other file of `public/assets` to the deployment, because `public/assets` keeps the files of earlier builds. <a id="HYC-16.8"></a> The static shell contains `<meta name="hyper-api">`, the inlined entry and no stylesheet, because the browser applies the stylesheet links of the rendered layout before it shows the page (HYC-8, HYC-15). <a id="HYC-16.9"></a> `tests/scripts/build-assets.test.mts` builds an application whose entry imports a module with `import()`.

## Kept data

- **HY-37** <a id="HY-37.1"></a> A route region may declare kept paths, because only route regions change in the browser (HY-30); the manifest check rejects `keep` on a manifest region. <a id="HY-37.2"></a> An example is `"keep": { "notice.closed": "server", "sort": "localStorage" }`. <a id="HY-37.3"></a> A path is a dotted path: a map key `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, then any number of `.` each followed by a map key or by a list index of decimal digits. <a id="HY-37.4"></a> A kept value survives a reload in the storage named by its kind:

| Kind | Storage | Request when the value changes | First SSR document |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `server` | the server session | one background request that rendering does not wait for | contains the value |
| `cookie` | the cookie `hy-keep`, written by the browser code; it cannot be `HttpOnly` | none | contains the value |
| `localStorage` | the browser `localStorage` | none | contains the loader value; the browser renders the kept value after it loads |
| `sessionStorage` | the browser `sessionStorage` of the tab | none | contains the loader value; the browser renders the kept value after it loads |
