- **HY-38** <a id="HY-38.1"></a> The value that the user set last in the browser takes precedence; the loader data is the default. <a id="HY-38.2"></a> A kept value conforms to the value at its path when the region data contains the path, the kept value is a value of the template data model (a number outside ±(2^53 − 1) is not), and:

  - <a id="HY-38.3"></a> a null, boolean, number or string has the same type;
  - <a id="HY-38.4"></a> a map replaces a map; when the data map has keys, the kept map has the same keys and the value of every key conforms to the value of the same key;
  - <a id="HY-38.5"></a> a list replaces a list; when the data list has items, every kept item conforms to its first item.

  <a id="HY-38.6"></a> An empty data map or list gives no shape, so any map or list conforms to it; the rendering check below covers such values.

  <a id="HY-38.7"></a> A kept value that does not conform is ignored.

  - <a id="HY-38.8"></a> The server reads `server` and `cookie` values and sends the conforming ones in `kept` (HY-17). <a id="HY-38.9"></a> They never change `regions`. <a id="HY-38.10"></a> It reads the `cookie` values from the cookie `__Host-hy-keep` when the request uses HTTPS or the application declares HTTPS (HY-45), and from `hy-keep` otherwise; on HTTPS the host-only cookie alone counts, because another host, such as a sibling subdomain, cannot set it. <a id="HY-38.11"></a> The cookie value is the URL-encoded JSON object `{ "<region>": { "<path>": <value> } }`.
  - <a id="HY-38.12"></a> A region renders with its kept values applied to its data in this order: the values in `kept`, the `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` values, and the `server` values whose saving has not completed (HYC-13). <a id="HY-38.13"></a> The server applies only the values in `kept`. <a id="HY-38.14"></a> The browser applies all of them to the data that it holds and renders, and does not synchronize them with the server. <a id="HY-38.15"></a> For a document rendered by the server, the browser applies them after it holds the embedded data, or after it obtains the data when a browser value is stored (HYC-4, HYC-7), and renders every region whose data changed.
  - <a id="HY-38.16"></a> When a region does not render alone (HY-13) with its kept values applied, it renders with its loader data, and its kept values are removed from `kept` and from the held data. <a id="HY-38.17"></a> The server removes them before it renders the embedded data (HY-31), so the server and the browser render the same document. <a id="HY-38.18"></a> When the region does not render with its loader data either, rendering fails (HY-43, HYC-14).

  <a id="HY-38.19"></a> A kept value takes the place of the value at its path, so every map of the data keeps its keys in their order, and a kept map keeps its keys in its own order.

- **HYC-13** <a id="HYC-13.1"></a> When `set`, `render` or `hy-set` changes a path, the browser renders the region first and then stores every kept path that equals the changed path, lies under it or contains it, with the value now at the kept path. <a id="HYC-13.2"></a> A `server` value stays pending until the server answers 204 for it or a later change of the same path is saved; while it is pending it is applied as in HY-38. <a id="HYC-13.3"></a> Saves of one path are sent one at a time: a change made while a save of its path is in flight is sent after that save completes, and only the latest value is sent. <a id="HYC-13.4"></a> A failed save keeps the value pending and marks the region as failed (HYC-14) when no later change of the path exists. <a id="HYC-13.5"></a> For `server` it sends `POST <base path>/_hyper/keep` with the form fields `_csrf` (the held `shared.csrf`, HY-10), `region`, `path` and `value` (the JSON text of the value) and does not wait for the response. <a id="HYC-13.6"></a> For `cookie` it writes the cookie `hy-keep` with `Path=/`, `SameSite=Lax` and `Max-Age` of one year; on HTTPS the cookie is `__Host-hy-keep` and also `Secure`, so that another host, such as a sibling subdomain, cannot set it. <a id="HYC-13.7"></a> The cookie value is the URL-encoded JSON object `{ "<region>": { "<path>": <value> } }`.

- **HY-40** <a id="HY-40.1"></a> The server answers `POST <base path>/_hyper/keep` with status 204 after it stores the value in the session, with status 403 when the CSRF token does not match, and with status 400 when the region does not declare the path as `server`, the value is not JSON, the JSON text is longer than 4,096 bytes, or the value is not a value of the template data model. <a id="HY-40.2"></a> The path `/_hyper/keep` is reserved; a route path may not start with `/_hyper`.

## Request boundary and failures

- **HY-42** <a id="HY-42.1"></a> The request path is the path of the request target: the target up to its first `?` or `#`, and for an absolute-form target (`http://host/path`) the part after the authority. <a id="HY-42.2"></a> It is not decoded further. <a id="HY-42.3"></a> The path must consist of the printable ASCII characters `!` to `~`, as RFC 9112 requires of a request target, and every query and form name and value (HY-56, HY-57) and the `HX-Current-URL` header must be valid UTF-8; otherwise the server responds with status 400 before any loader or action runs. <a id="HY-42.4"></a> Cookies are not checked: the server ignores a `hy-keep` cookie that is not a JSON object, ignores its values that do not conform (HY-38), and starts a new session for a session cookie that is not an identifier that it created (HY-45). <a id="HY-42.5"></a> A leading U+FEFF of a decoded query or form name or value (HY-56), of a route parameter (HY-5) and of a cookie value (HY-129) is a character of it, which no server and no browser code removes.

- **HY-43** <a id="HY-43.1"></a> An exception that the application does not handle produces status 500 with the text `Internal Server Error`. <a id="HY-43.2"></a> The response contains no exception message, file path or stack trace; the server writes them to its log. <a id="HY-43.3"></a> The PHP setting `display_errors` must be off before PHP starts the request, because PHP writes startup warnings (for example `max_input_vars`) before the application runs.

- **HY-74** <a id="HY-74.1"></a> While a server answers a request, a warning that its runtime raises becomes an error, and the request fails with HY-43. <a id="HY-74.2"></a> The runtime would otherwise continue, and the server would send a wrong page with status 200 while the message reaches only the log or the output. <a id="HY-74.3"></a> An error that an expression silences stays silent. <a id="HY-74.4"></a> The server installs its handling for the requests only and restores the previous handling afterwards.

  - <a id="HY-74.5"></a> PHP: every warning, notice and deprecation that PHP raises, such as an undefined variable, an undefined array key or a wrong argument, becomes an exception through an error handler; an error that `@` silences is not in `error_reporting()` and stays silent.
  - <a id="HY-74.6"></a> Python: every warning of the `warnings` module that is raised while a request is answered, such as a `DeprecationWarning` or a `RuntimeWarning`, is raised as an exception: the filter `error` is set while a request is in flight.
  - <a id="HY-74.7"></a> Node: a warning that is emitted with `process.emitWarning` while a request is answered throws its error at the call.

- **HY-44** <a id="HY-44.1"></a> Shared data and region data are values of the template data model. <a id="HY-44.2"></a> A number outside ±(2^53 − 1), integer or not, fails with HY-43, for a document and for JSON alike. <a id="HY-44.3"></a> The server checks every value that the context handler (HY-124), the shared handler and the loaders return before it removes the values that no template reads (HY-73), so a value outside the data model fails also when no template reads it. <a id="HY-44.4"></a> The context handler (HY-124), the shared handler and every loader return a map: in PHP an array that is empty or is not a list, in Python a `dict`, and in Node a `Map` for the context handler and a plain object or a `Map` for the shared handler and every loader. <a id="HY-44.5"></a> Another value, such as a list, fails with HY-43. <a id="HY-44.6"></a> The check is the host binding of the template data model (VAL-13, VAL-14) followed by a check that the bound value holds no native object (VAL-19): a value that binding turns into a value of the data model passes, such as a PHP `stdClass` or `JsonSerializable` and a Node plain object, and an application object that binding keeps as a native object, such as a PHP `DateTimeImmutable`, a Node `Date` or a Python `datetime`, fails with HY-43 on every server. <a id="HY-44.7"></a> A JSON response checks only the parameters of the request again, because this check covered the shared data and the region data and a kept value enters a response only when it is a value of the data model (HY-38). <a id="HY-44.8"></a> A value outside the data model fails with an error of the classes of HY-46.2 whose message names the kind of the failure: `a number outside ±(2^53 − 1) is not a value of the data model (HY-44)`, `a number that is not finite is not a value of the data model (HY-44)`, `a string that is not UTF-8 text is not a value of the data model (HY-44)`, `lists and maps that nest deeper than 64 levels are not a value of the data model (HY-44)` and, for any other value or map key, `a value or a map key of another type is not a value of the data model (HY-44)`.

- **HY-45** <a id="HY-45.1"></a> The server session cookie is named `__Host-hy-session` when the request uses HTTPS or when the application declares that it is served over HTTPS, which a server behind a TLS-terminating proxy must do, and `hy-session` otherwise; the application does not choose the name. <a id="HY-45.2"></a> The browser accepts a `__Host-` cookie only from its own host, so another host, such as a sibling subdomain, cannot give a visitor a session whose token it knows. <a id="HY-45.3"></a> The cookie has `Path=/`, no `Domain`, `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Lax`, and it is `Secure` under the same condition as the prefix. <a id="HY-45.4"></a> The server accepts only session identifiers that it created, and starts a session only when a request reads or writes session data: a request that the server rejects before routing (HY-42) or whose path matches no route creates no session. <a id="HY-45.5"></a> Every response carries `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors <sources>`, where the application sets the sources and the default is `'self'`.

- **HY-46** <a id="HY-46.1"></a> A redirect location is an application path: valid UTF-8 that starts with `/`, whose second character is neither `/` nor `\`, that contains no control character (C0, DEL or C1), no space and no `\`, and whose path has no segment `.` or `..`, also when a dot is percent-encoded (`%2e`). <a id="HY-46.2"></a> Making a redirect to a location that is not an application path fails with the error `a redirect location is not an application path (HY-46)`, of the class `InvalidArgumentException` in PHP, `RangeError` in Node and `ValueError` in Python.

- **HYC-14** <a id="HYC-14.1"></a> When a region request receives a response that is not JSON, or when rendering, saving a kept value, loading templates or loading a stylesheet (HYC-15) fails, the browser does not swap and does not change history. <a id="HYC-14.2"></a> It sets the attribute `hy-error` on the region element to the response status, or to `0` for a network or rendering failure, and removes the attribute from every region that renders successfully afterwards. <a id="HYC-14.3"></a> A cancelled request is not a failure; a request that htmx aborts because its timeout (`hx-timeout`, or `htmx.config.defaultTimeout`) passed is a network failure. <a id="HYC-14.4"></a> `render`, `set` and `hy-set` change held data only after the region rendered; a failure leaves held data unchanged. <a id="HYC-14.5"></a> When client-side rendering of a document fails, or a stylesheet of a history restoration in server-side rendering fails to load, the browser sets `hy-error` on the body.

- **HY-129** <a id="HY-129.1"></a> The cookies of a request are the result of one parse of its `Cookie` header, the same in every server. <a id="HY-129.2"></a> The header is the bytes of its field value as received. <a id="HY-129.3"></a> A client sends one `Cookie` line (RFC 6265 section 5.4), and over HTTP/2 the server joins the cookie lines with `; ` (RFC 9113 section 8.2.3). <a id="HY-129.4"></a> A host that receives the lines apart joins them with `; ` before the parse: the Node server takes `cookie` of `node:http`, which joins with `; `, the Python `create_server` reads every `Cookie` line, and the Python ASGI callable joins the `cookie` headers of the scope with `; `. <a id="HY-129.5"></a> A host that receives the header joined takes it as given: PHP takes `$_SERVER['HTTP_COOKIE']` from its SAPI, and the Python WSGI callable takes `HTTP_COOKIE` and encodes it in Latin-1 back to its bytes. <a id="HY-129.6"></a> The PHP built-in server joins several HTTP/1.1 `Cookie` lines with `, `, so such a request, which breaks RFC 6265 section 5.4, gives the cookies of that joined value. <a id="HY-129.7"></a> The header splits at each `;` into pairs, spaces and tabs at both ends of a pair are removed, and a pair splits at its first `=` into a name and a value. <a id="HY-129.8"></a> A pair gives no cookie when it has no `=`, when its name is empty, when its name is not valid UTF-8, or when its value after percent-decoding is not valid UTF-8; the name is not decoded, and the value is percent-decoded, where `%` with two hexadecimal digits is the byte of those digits and every other byte, `+` included, is itself. <a id="HY-129.9"></a> Of the pairs that give a cookie, the first of a name counts. <a id="HY-129.10"></a> No part of the PHP server reads `$_COOKIE`, whose names PHP changes as the names of its variables (`a.b` becomes `a_b`, and `a[x]` an array): its native session runs with `session.use_cookies` set to false, receives the identifier of HY-45 from this parse with `session_id()` before `session_start()`, or none when the parse gives no identifier, and the server sends the session cookie of HY-45 itself. <a id="HY-129.12"></a> The cookies of a request are a map from names to values.

- **HY-130** <a id="HY-130.19"></a> A response of an application carries the headers that the rules of this document name for it, and may carry other headers unless a rule states that it has no other header; the host of a server may add headers to any response. <a id="HY-130.20"></a> A header name has no case: names that differ only in ASCII case are one name (RFC 9110 section 5.1).

## Node server

- **HY-54** <a id="HY-54.1"></a> The Node server package `@polyspec/hyper-server` implements the server rules of this document as the PHP server does; its tests run the cases of the PHP server tests against the same fixtures. <a id="HY-54.2"></a> It differs from the PHP server only as follows:

  - <a id="HY-54.3"></a> It renders a document as the browser renders the document JSON value (HY-12, HY-31, HY-38), with the browser code and the template files of the asset build (HR-34), and embeds its data when the reply asks for it (HY-92).
  - <a id="HY-54.4"></a> Its JSON text has the bytes of PHP `json_encode` with `JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES`. <a id="HY-54.5"></a> A string escapes `"`, `\`, the control characters below U+0020 (`\b`, `\f`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, and `\u00xx` for the others) and U+2028 and U+2029 (`\u2028`, `\u2029`), and no other character. <a id="HY-54.6"></a> An integer within ±(2^53 − 1) is written in decimal. <a id="HY-54.7"></a> Another number is written with the shortest digits that read back as the same number: positionally when its decimal point position p (the number is 0.d × 10^p) is between −3 and 17, and otherwise as `d.ddde±x` with at least one fraction digit; negative zero is `-0`. <a id="HY-54.8"></a> It decodes kept values (HY-38, HY-40) as PHP `json_decode` does: an integer literal is an integer and other literals are floats, a number outside ±(2^53 − 1) or one that is not finite is not a value of the data model, and 512 nested containers, a lone surrogate escape or a key that starts with U+0000 fail.
  - <a id="HY-54.12"></a> A JavaScript value of the data model is null, a boolean, a number or a bigint within ±(2^53 − 1), a string, an array, a `Map` with string keys or a plain object. <a id="HY-54.13"></a> A string with a lone surrogate, which has no UTF-8 form, and any other value fail with HY-43.
  - <a id="HY-54.14"></a> Loaders and actions receive one context argument with the request, the reply (HY-52) and the services that the application binds by key.
  - <a id="HY-54.15"></a> Its session store keeps each session in a file of one directory, named by an identifier of 64 hexadecimal digits that the store created. <a id="HY-54.16"></a> It writes the session cookie with the attributes and the order of the PHP session cookie (`<name>=<id>; path=/; secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax`, `secure` under the conditions of HY-45), and it runs the requests of one session one after another.

- **HY-97** <a id="HY-97.1"></a> Every server takes an optional request hook `around`: an argument of `create_server`, `create_wsgi` and `create_asgi` (Python), an option of `App.listener` and `App.server` (Node), and an argument of `App::open` (PHP). <a id="HY-97.2"></a> The server calls it once for every request that it gives to the application, with the request as the server built it and a function `answer`, and sends the response that `around` returns. <a id="HY-97.3"></a> `answer(request)` runs the application for a request as the server does without `around`: it calls `App.handle` with the request and the session store of the server; `App.handle` opens the session of the request by its session cookie as HY-120 states, calls the response hook (HY-60) and closes the session, and `answer` returns the response with the cookie of a new session first (HY-45). <a id="HY-97.4"></a> `around` may call `answer` with the request or with a changed copy, such as a copy with a header that `Request.with_header(name, value)` (Python), `request.withHeader(name, value)` (Node) or `Request::withHeader($name, $value)` (PHP) sets (the name is compared without case, as a request reads a header); it may change the response that `answer` returns; and it may return its own response without calling `answer`, and then the server opens no session and runs no loader, action or hook of the application for that request. <a id="HY-97.5"></a> When a write of the response fails because the client closed the connection (HY-67), the server calls the disconnect hook with the request and the reply of the last call of `answer`, and does not call it when `around` did not call `answer`. <a id="HY-97.6"></a> The files of the public directory, which the Python and Node servers serve, are served before `around` and do not reach it. <a id="HY-97.7"></a> A value of `around` that is not callable fails when the server is created. <a id="HY-97.8"></a> An error that `around` raises outside `answer`, and a return value that is not a response, are escaped errors (HY-60), also for PHP, where `App::run` writes the plain 500 of an uncaught exception: the server logs them and answers the plain 500, which the write hook receives (HY-99).

  - <a id="HY-97.9"></a> The Node server gives the same through the `node:http` server that `app.server()` returns: a consumer replaces its `request` listener with a listener that calls the listener of the application, so that it runs each request in a context of its own, adds a request id header to the request and the response, or answers a request itself before the application, such as a 400 for a request that did not come from its web server. <a id="HY-97.10"></a> `around` gives these to an application of the Python server, whose `http.server` request handler is not replaceable.

- **HY-99** <a id="HY-99.1"></a> Every server takes an optional write hook `written`: an argument of `create_server`, `create_wsgi` and `create_asgi` (Python), an option of `App.listener` and `App.server` (Node), and an argument of `App::open` (PHP). <a id="HY-99.2"></a> The server calls it exactly once for each request that it gives to the application, with these values: the request that it gave to `around` (HY-97), or the request as received; the `Response` whose write it started, the plain 500 of an escaped error when none started, or null when the request ended before a response started; `ended`, which says whether the status line, the headers and the complete body were written without an error; the elapsed milliseconds since the arrival of the request (HY-60); and `failure`, the message of an escaped error as HY-43 states it, or null for every other response. <a id="HY-99.3"></a> It calls the hook after the answer of the request has ended (the application returned, failed or stopped on a closed connection, HY-67) and after the write ended or failed, whichever is later, and before the disconnect hook. <a id="HY-99.4"></a> An escaped error whose 500 cannot be written, because the response has started or the connection is closed, is reported with `ended` false and its failure. <a id="HY-99.5"></a> No adapter reports the plain 500 of an escaped error to the response hook. <a id="HY-99.6"></a> PHP calls the hook from a shutdown function that `App::run` registers after its escape function; `ended` is false when `connection_aborted()` is 1 or a fatal error ended the script after the headers were sent, and true means that PHP gave the complete output to the web server. <a id="HY-99.7"></a> Under either output buffering mode, `ended` and the response follow what PHP sent: with output buffering on and no output flushed, a fatal error after `App::run` replaces the response with the plain 500, which the hook receives with `ended` true; with output buffering off, or after a flush that sent the headers, the hook receives the started response with `ended` false. <a id="HY-99.8"></a> Node calls it after the `close` event of the `node:http` response and the end of the answer, with `ended` equal to `writableFinished`; the listener that `App.listener(sessions, options)` returns, which `App.server` installs, returns a promise that settles after the write hook and the disconnect hook of the request have run. <a id="HY-99.9"></a> WSGI: `ended` is true when the server consumes the whole body iterable, and false when it calls `close` before the end, also before the first item; an error before `start_response` is an escaped error, and so is a `start_response` that raises. <a id="HY-99.10"></a> ASGI: `ended` is true when both sends return, and false when a send raises or the task is cancelled; the error or the cancellation propagates. <a id="HY-99.11"></a> A request that ends before a response started, because its connection closed (HY-67), its task was cancelled (HY-100), or PHP `exit()` ended it without output, gives the hook a null response, with `ended` false and a null `failure` unless an error escaped. <a id="HY-99.12"></a> The hook is not called in three cases: for the files of the public directory, for a request that the transport gives no request to report (HY-60), and when the process ends before the request ends (a kill, or a worker timeout that ends the worker), because no code of the server runs then. <a id="HY-99.13"></a> An error that the hook raises is not handled by HY-43; it reaches the transport.

- **HY-100** <a id="HY-100.1"></a> Every server is served through the standard host interface of its runtime, and a host answers each request as the server does (HY-97, HY-99): PHP through a front controller that calls `App::run` under a SAPI (the built-in server or php-fpm), Python through the WSGI callable of `create_wsgi`, the ASGI callable of `create_asgi` or the `http.server` server of `create_server`, and Node through the `node:http` request listener of `App.listener`, which `App.server` installs. <a id="HY-100.2"></a> A host reads the request body up to the body limit of the application and no more (HY-59), passes its session store to `App.handle`, which opens the session as HY-120 states, sets the cookie of a new session first (HY-45), runs the request hook `around` (HY-97), reports the write to the write hook (HY-99) and a closed connection to the disconnect hook (HY-67), and answers a request whose target it cannot give with the plain 500 of HY-60.

  - <a id="HY-100.3"></a> Python WSGI: `polyspec.hyper.wsgi.create_wsgi(app, sessions, files=None, around=None, written=None)` of the Python server `polyspec-hyper-server` takes the arguments of `create_server` (HY-97, HY-99) and returns a WSGI application callable (PEP 3333) that a WSGI server runs. <a id="HY-100.4"></a> The callable answers every request as `create_server` does: it serves the files of the public directory before `around`, reads the request body up to the body limit of the application and no more (HY-59), passes its session store to `App.handle`, which opens the session as HY-120 states, sets the cookie of a new session first (HY-45) and runs the request hook `around` (HY-97). <a id="HY-100.5"></a> It adds the header `Content-Length` of the complete body itself. <a id="HY-100.6"></a> The write hook `written` (HY-99) reports that the write ended when the WSGI server consumed the whole body iterable, and that it failed when the server closed the iterable before its end, which PEP 3333 defines as premature termination; when the write failed, the callable calls the disconnect hook (HY-67) with the request that it gave to `around` and the reply of the last call of `answer`. <a id="HY-100.7"></a> The hook is not called for the files of the public directory. <a id="HY-100.8"></a> An error that `around` raises outside `answer`, or a value that it returns that is not a `Response`, is an escaped error (HY-60): the callable answers the plain 500 before it calls `start_response`, and the write hook receives it. <a id="HY-100.9"></a> An error that `start_response` raises, and a status, a header or a body that the callable cannot encode, is an escaped error too: the callable passes the plain 500 to `start_response` with the exception information of the error (PEP 3333), and the write hook receives it with its `failure`. <a id="HY-100.10"></a> The request target is the one that the WSGI server received. <a id="HY-100.11"></a> PEP 3333 has no raw path, so the callable reads the target from `RAW_URI` (gunicorn) or else from `REQUEST_URI` (uWSGI, mod_wsgi). <a id="HY-100.12"></a> The request path is the target up to its first `?`, and the raw query is the text after its first `?` (HY-42, HY-56), split as `create_server` splits its target. <a id="HY-100.13"></a> The callable never reads `PATH_INFO`, which the server has percent-decoded, and never re-encodes it. <a id="HY-100.14"></a> When the environ has neither key, the request has no target to report: the callable logs an error that names `RAW_URI` and `REQUEST_URI`, and answers the plain 500 of HY-60 before it calls `start_response`.
  - <a id="HY-100.15"></a> Python ASGI: `polyspec.hyper.asgi.create_asgi(app, sessions, files=None, around=None, written=None)` of the Python server `polyspec-hyper-server` takes the arguments of `create_server` (HY-97, HY-99) and returns an ASGI 3 application callable that an ASGI server runs. <a id="HY-100.16"></a> The callable answers every request of the scope type `http` as `create_server` does: the public files before `around`, the request body read up to the body limit of the application and no more (HY-59), the session cookie of a new session first (HY-45) and the request hook `around` (HY-97). <a id="HY-100.17"></a> It runs the pipeline of a request in a worker thread, so the event loop of the server answers other requests while a request responds. <a id="HY-100.18"></a> It sends one `http.response.start` with the status and the headers of the `Response` and one `http.response.body` with the complete body: the write hook `written` (HY-99) reports that the write ended when both sends return, and that it failed when a send raises, which an ASGI server does for a connection that the client closed; when the write failed, the callable calls `written`, then the disconnect hook (HY-67) with the request that it gave to `around` and the reply of the last call of `answer`, and lets the error propagate to the server. <a id="HY-100.19"></a> A cancellation of the task reports `written` with `ended` false and propagates the cancellation, without the disconnect hook, because the cancellation does not state that the client closed the connection. <a id="HY-100.20"></a> As `create_server` does (HY-67), the callable learns of a closed connection only when a send fails; it does not watch the `http.disconnect` message. <a id="HY-100.21"></a> The hook is not called for the files of the public directory. <a id="HY-100.22"></a> The library names no server; a deployment runs the callable with the server that it chooses. <a id="HY-100.23"></a> The request path is `scope['raw_path']` decoded as latin-1: the raw bytes of the target path without the query, which the ASGI specification defines; it is split as HY-42 splits a target. <a id="HY-100.24"></a> The raw query is `scope['query_string']` decoded as latin-1 (HY-56). <a id="HY-100.25"></a> The callable never builds the path from `scope['path']`, which the server has percent-decoded. <a id="HY-100.26"></a> An ASGI server that omits `raw_path`, which the specification makes optional, makes the request have no target to report: the callable logs an error that names `raw_path`, and sends the plain 500 of HY-60 before it sends anything. <a id="HY-100.27"></a> When a send of that 500 fails, the callable calls `written` with the failed write and lets the error propagate to the server, as HY-67 does for a failed send.
  - <a id="HY-100.28"></a> Node: `App.listener(sessions, options)` of the Node server returns the `node:http` request listener that `App.server` installs. <a id="HY-100.29"></a> The listener returns a promise that settles after the write hook and the disconnect hook of the request have run (HY-99).
  - <a id="HY-100.30"></a> PHP: `App::run` is the entry of the front controller; it turns `ignore_user_abort` off, registers the shutdown function that calls the write hook and the disconnect hook (HY-67, HY-99), and writes the plain 500 of an uncaught exception or a fatal error (HY-60).

## Errors

- **HY-27** <a id="HY-27.1"></a> A path without a route, or a loader that reports a missing resource, responds with status 404. <a id="HY-27.2"></a> A method other than `GET` or a declared `POST` responds with status 405; a representation checks the method of HY-121 instead. <a id="HY-27.3"></a> A loader or an action reports a missing resource with the not-found stop, whose message is `not found`; the forbidden stop of HY-51 has the message `forbidden` and the bad-request stop of HY-58 the message `bad request`.

- **HY-50** <a id="HY-50.1"></a> A loader or an action may stop the request with a redirect: it throws the redirect of a result of HY-25, which names an application path (HY-46) and may carry flash values and changed topics. <a id="HY-50.2"></a> The server responds with status 303 and `Location` with the base path, stores the flash values and the changed topics as HY-25 does, and renders nothing. <a id="HY-50.3"></a> Making a redirect stop of a result that is not a redirect fails with the error `a redirect stop needs a redirect result (HY-50)`, of the classes of HY-46.2; the message of a redirect stop is `redirect to` followed by a space and its location.

- **HY-51** <a id="HY-51.1"></a> A loader or an action may stop the request as forbidden. <a id="HY-51.2"></a> The server responds with status 403 and the text `Forbidden`, and runs no other loader or action of the request.

- **HY-52** <a id="HY-52.1"></a> Every loader and action of a request may receive the reply of the request. <a id="HY-52.2"></a> The reply adds a cookie with a name of `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*` that does not start with `hy-`, a value of the characters `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -` and an optional `Max-Age`, or removes a cookie with `Max-Age=0`. <a id="HY-52.3"></a> Each such cookie has `Path=/`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax` and `Secure` under the conditions of HY-45. <a id="HY-52.4"></a> Another name or value fails with HY-43. <a id="HY-52.5"></a> A page response has `Cache-Control: no-store`; the reply may set the `Cache-Control` of a page response with status 200, and its value replaces `no-store`. <a id="HY-52.6"></a> A page carries the session token of its visitor (HY-10, HY-24), so a value without the directive `private` or `no-store`, or with `public` or `s-maxage`, fails with HY-43: a shared cache must not give the page of one visitor to another. <a id="HY-52.7"></a> The server session adds only its cookie to a response, and no caching header. <a id="HY-52.8"></a> A response without a body, a 304 of HY-53 included, has no `Content-Type`. <a id="HY-52.9"></a> The response of the request contains the cookies of its reply, whether it is a page, a redirect or a failure of HY-27, HY-50 or HY-51. <a id="HY-52.10"></a> A `Max-Age` is an integer of the data model that is not negative: a number within ±(2^53 − 1) without a fraction, so that `60.0` is the integer 60 and a bool is not an integer. <a id="HY-52.11"></a> A cookie name, a cookie value or a `Cache-Control` value that is not a string, and a `Max-Age` that is neither null nor such an integer, fail with `TypeError` and the message `a cookie name is not a string (HY-52)`, `a cookie value is not a string (HY-52)`, `a Cache-Control is not a string (HY-52)` or `a Max-Age is not an integer within ±(2^53 − 1) (HY-52)`, and the types of a cookie are checked in the order of its parameters before its values. <a id="HY-52.12"></a> A cookie of these types fails otherwise with the class of HY-46.2 and the message `cookie name <name> is not allowed (HY-52)`, `cookie value of <name> has a character that is not allowed (HY-52)` or `cookie <name> has a negative Max-Age (HY-52)` in this order, and a `Cache-Control` string with the message `Cache-Control has a character that is not allowed (HY-52)` or `Cache-Control <value> lets a shared cache store the page; it needs private or no-store and neither public nor s-maxage (HY-52)`, where `<name>` and `<value>` are the given strings.

- **HY-105** <a id="HY-105.1"></a> Loaders, actions and representation handlers (HY-121) receive the services that the application binds. <a id="HY-105.2"></a> The application binds a factory for a service; the server calls the factory on the first use of the service and gives the same service to every later handler of the application. <a id="HY-105.3"></a> A service without a factory fails the request with HY-43. <a id="HY-105.4"></a> A handler names a service by the class of a parameter in PHP and Python, and by the key that it passes to `services.get` in Node.

- **HY-106** <a id="HY-106.1"></a> The public API of a server is what an application and a host use, and every part of it exists in the PHP, Python and Node servers, each under the form of its runtime: the application (`App`, its `open`, `bind` and `handle`) and the host entries of HY-100; the request (HY-56, HY-57, HY-96), the reply (HY-52, HY-103), the response and the result of HY-25 with the stops of HY-50, HY-51 and HY-58 (`Redirect`, `Forbidden`, `NotFound`, `BadRequest`); the session stores of HY-104 and HY-115 and the session store interface; the context handler (HY-124): PHP `App::open(context: \Closure(mixed $selection): array)`, Python `App.open(context=...)` with a function of the selection value that returns a `dict`, and the Node option `context`, a function of the selection value that returns a `Map` or a promise of one; the host functions (HYC-24): `functions`, a map from names to functions, an argument of PHP `App::open` and Python `App.open` and an option of Node `App.open` and of the browser `HyperOptions`; the representation handlers (HY-118): `representations` in the handlers of a route, a map from the `type`, exactly as the manifest writes it, to its handler, which receives what a loader receives without the reply, and the media type of the selection (HY-119): PHP and Python by the parameter types `Request`, `MediaType` and those of its services (HY-105), and Node one context argument `{ request, media, services }`; `MediaType` has `parameters()` (PHP, Python) or `parameters` (Node), an ordered map from each required parameter name, as `parameters` declares it, to its selected value, and `etag(body)` (HY-122); the handler returns a `Representation` (PHP `new Representation(status:, body:, headers:)`, Python `Representation(status, body, headers)`, Node `new Representation(status, body, headers)`, with a null body for none), a Node handler a promise of it as well; and `json()` of the request (HY-121); the services of HY-105; and the client rendering and its choice (HY-34). <a id="HY-106.2"></a> Every other symbol that a package declares is internal: PHP marks it with the docblock tag `@internal`, Python names it with a leading underscore (its module included), and Node marks it with `@internal` in its documentation comment, which `stripInternal` removes from the declarations, or does not export it. <a id="HY-106.3"></a> The tests of a package use internal symbols freely, and no application relies on them. <a id="HY-106.4"></a> PHP request query, form and file maps expose the native `IteratorAggregate` interface and iterate names and value lists in contract order; their concrete storage classes remain internal. <a id="HY-106.5"></a> Public upload metadata, bytes, construction, the request file-limit predicate and the application file-limit option exist in each runtime form. <a id="HY-106.6"></a> An application that fails to open raises the open error of its runtime, of exactly that class: `InvalidArgumentException` in PHP, `Error` in Node and `ValueError` in Python, also when a file that it reads is not valid JSON or not valid UTF-8; only the build file (HY-125.5), when it is missing, not readable, not valid UTF-8 or JSON, or does not hold a build id, raises the subclass `InvalidBuild` of that class. <a id="HY-106.7"></a> A file that starts with U+FEFF is not valid JSON, because JSON allows no character before a value. <a id="HY-106.8"></a> A call of a public method with another number of arguments than its parameters is outside the public API: each runtime answers it by its own calling convention, so that PHP and Python fail it with their `TypeError` and its own message, Node and PHP ignore an extra argument and Node gives a missing argument as `undefined`, and the errors and messages that the rules state hold for a call that gives each parameter.

- **HY-107** <a id="HY-107.1"></a> A loader or an action may let an error of the ORM escape, and the server answers it as the stop of its meaning, so that a handler calls the ORM directly. <a id="HY-107.2"></a> The server identifies the error without a dependency on the ORM, by the name of its class, `OrmException` in PHP and `OrmError` in Node and Python, and by its string code, the property `code_` in PHP and `code` in Node and Python. <a id="HY-107.3"></a> The code `NO_ROWS`, a strict query for one row that matched no row, is answered as `NotFound` (HY-27: status 404 and the text `Not Found`). <a id="HY-107.4"></a> The code `REVISION_CHANGED`, a write with an expected revision that found the row at another revision or no row, is answered, when an action raises it, as the page of the route with status 409 and no data of its own (HY-58); a loader that raises it fails with HY-43, because the page cannot load. <a id="HY-107.5"></a> Every other error of the ORM, and every error of another kind, is not handled by this rule and fails with HY-43. <a id="HY-107.6"></a> A handler that wants another answer catches the error itself.

- **HY-53** <a id="HY-53.1"></a> A JSON response with status 200 has a weak `ETag`, `W/"<digits>"`, made of the first 32 hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 digest of its body after every occurrence of the masked token of the response is replaced by the session token (HY-24). <a id="HY-53.2"></a> Two responses with the same data and the same session token therefore have the same tag although their masks differ, and the tag is weak because their bytes differ (RFC 9110, section 8.8.1). <a id="HY-53.3"></a> A renewed session (HY-72) has another token and so another tag. <a id="HY-53.4"></a> A `GET` request whose `If-None-Match` header equals that tag receives status 304 with the headers of the 200 response except `Content-Type` and no body, because a 304 carries no representation (RFC 9110, section 15.4.5) and php-fpm removes the `Content-Type` of a 304; an action runs whatever tag its request names.

- **HY-103** <a id="HY-103.1"></a> A loader or an action may set the `Referrer-Policy` of the page and JSON answers of its request with `Reply::referrerPolicy(value)` in PHP, `reply.referrerPolicy(value)` in Node and `reply.referrer_policy(value)` in Python. <a id="HY-103.2"></a> The value is one of the tokens of the Referrer-Policy specification, compared exactly: `no-referrer`, `no-referrer-when-downgrade`, `origin`, `origin-when-cross-origin`, `same-origin`, `strict-origin`, `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` and `unsafe-url`. <a id="HY-103.3"></a> Another value fails with HY-43, as a `Cache-Control` value without `private` or `no-store` does (HY-52). <a id="HY-103.4"></a> A later call replaces the value. <a id="HY-103.5"></a> Every page and JSON answer of the request, whatever its status, then has the header `Referrer-Policy` with that value, and so does a 304 of HY-53. <a id="HY-103.6"></a> Without such a call a page or JSON answer has no `Referrer-Policy` from the reply. <a id="HY-103.7"></a> The method sets no other header, and the redirects, the stops and the plain text failures of HY-27, HY-50, HY-51 and HY-65 have none from the reply. <a id="HY-103.8"></a> A value that is not a string fails with `TypeError` and the message `a Referrer-Policy is not a string (HY-103)`, and another string fails with the class of HY-46.2 and the message `Referrer-Policy <value> is not a token of the Referrer-Policy specification (HY-103)`.

- **HY-104** <a id="HY-104.1"></a> The PHP, Node and Python servers that share one session directory share its sessions, and so do the processes of one server. <a id="HY-104.2"></a> A session is the file `sess_<id>` of the directory, the form of the files handler of PHP: its bytes are the record of its values in the form `php_serialize` of PHP, read and written with `@polyspec/php-serialize` and `polyspec-php-serialize`, its mode is 0600, and a file without bytes is an empty session. <a id="HY-104.3"></a> The requests of one session run one after another in every process and no write is lost: each server holds `flock` with `LOCK_EX` on the session file from the opening of the session of a request to its closing, and a representation request, which opens no session (HY-120), holds no lock, and the operating system releases the lock of a process that ended. <a id="HY-104.4"></a> The PHP server keeps a session with the native session handler of PHP, with `serialize_handler` set to `php_serialize` by its session options. <a id="HY-104.5"></a> The Python server blocks on `fcntl.flock`. <a id="HY-104.6"></a> The Node server calls `flock` through `node:ffi` with `LOCK_NB` and tries again after a pause of at most 50 ms, because a call that blocks would stop its event loop. <a id="HY-104.7"></a> The server writes a record over the file in place under the lock and cuts the file to its length, as PHP does, so a process that ends during a write can leave a record that the next request cannot read; a request that changed nothing keeps the bytes and sets a new modification time. <a id="HY-104.8"></a> Only a missing session file starts a new session: a session file that the server cannot read or decode fails the request with its error (HY-60). <a id="HY-104.9"></a> An identifier is 22 to 128 characters of `A-Za-z0-9,-`: the Python and Node servers create 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, PHP creates its own, and each accepts the identifier of another. <a id="HY-104.10"></a> An identifier without a file names no session and creates no file. <a id="HY-104.11"></a> A renewal (HY-72) creates the new file before it removes the old one, and a request that waited for the lock of a removed file starts a new session. <a id="HY-104.12"></a> A value that a request did not set stays as it was read. <a id="HY-104.13"></a> A Node or Python server reads a record as the data model: an integer key is its decimal text, a float its number, a `stdClass` a map and a reference its value, and a list where the session keeps a map is that map, because a PHP array with the keys 0 to n-1 reads as a list. <a id="HY-104.14"></a> It writes an empty map and a map with the keys 0 to n-1 as a `stdClass`, so that every server reads it as a map; a record that holds an object of another class fails the request. <a id="HY-104.15"></a> The removal of expired sessions skips a session whose lock a request holds. <a id="HY-104.16"></a> `tests/scripts/session-shared.test.mts` checks it with processes of the three servers on one session, and `NativeSessionTest.php`, `packages/server/python/tests/test_file_sessions.py` and `packages/server/ts/tests/sessions-race.test.ts` with several processes of one server.

- **HY-115** <a id="HY-115.1"></a> The PHP, Node and Python servers that share one Redis server share its sessions, with the protocol of phpredis 6.3.0, and so do the processes of one server. <a id="HY-115.2"></a> A session is the key `PHPREDIS_SESSION:<id>`, whose bytes are the record of HY-104 and which expires after the lifetime of the session. <a id="HY-115.3"></a> The requests of one session run one after another in every process: a request takes the lock `<key>_LOCK` with `SET NX PX`, tries it again after a pause while another holds it, and fails with status 500 (HY-43) when its tries end, in every server and whatever `error_reporting` keeps. <a id="HY-115.4"></a> A request that opens a session reads it after it holds the lock, and one whose key is gone by then starts a new session. <a id="HY-115.5"></a> A lock expires so that a process that ended cannot hold it for ever, so a holder compares the value of the lock with its own secret before it writes with `SETEX`: a request that lost its lock writes nothing. <a id="HY-115.6"></a> The Node and Python servers close the session before they answer, so such a request fails with status 500 (HY-43); the PHP server closes it after the response, so phpredis writes a warning to the log and the response stands. <a id="HY-115.7"></a> A request that changed nothing keeps the bytes and sets a new expiry with `EXPIRE` without comparing the lock, because it writes no record, so a long request that only reads does not fail when its lock expires. <a id="HY-115.8"></a> A request releases its lock with the script that compares the value and deletes the key, so it never releases the lock of another. <a id="HY-115.9"></a> A PHP server sets `session.save_handler=redis`, `session.save_path`, `redis.session.locking_enabled=1` and `redis.session.lock_expire`, which must be set because a lock without an expiry outlives its process when `max_execution_time` is 0. <a id="HY-115.10"></a> The Node and Python servers take a function that runs one command on a client of the application and returns a bulk string as bytes, and the options `lockExpire`, `lockRetries` and `lockWait` (Python `lock_expire`, `lock_retries`, `lock_wait`), which mean what those of phpredis mean; every server of one Redis server gives them the same values, and the expiry is longer than any request. <a id="HY-115.11"></a> A renewal (HY-72) writes the new key before it deletes the old one, and the rules of identifiers and values of HY-104 hold. <a id="HY-115.12"></a> A request that cannot reach the Redis server answers status 500 (HY-43) in every server, tells no detail and sets no session cookie, so the client keeps its session, and the sessions that the Redis server kept go on after it starts again; a process that ended while it held a lock delays the requests of that session until the lock expires and wrote nothing. <a id="HY-115.13"></a> `tests/scripts/session-shared-redis.test.mts` checks it with processes of the three servers on a real Redis server, the PHP server through real phpredis, and `tests/scripts/session-redis-failure.test.mts` with a lock that really expires, a killed process, the HTTP servers of the board and a stop and a start of the Redis server. <a id="HY-115.14"></a> On a primary with replicas, a server reaches the primary that Redis Sentinel names, the PHP server through `RedisSentinelSessions`, which sets `session.save_path` before the session starts and leaves the session module of phpredis in place. <a id="HY-115.15"></a> The Python server asks Sentinel through the `setup` option of `RedisSessions` before the first command of a request that has a session, because a pooled connection of redis-py stays on the former primary, which accepts writes for some seconds after a promotion. <a id="HY-115.16"></a> A request answers status 500 (HY-43) while no primary answers and the session goes on after a promotion; a failover keeps what a replica acknowledged and can lose what it did not receive, because replication is asynchronous. <a id="HY-115.17"></a> The connections take TLS and an ACL user in every server. <a id="HY-115.18"></a> `tests/scripts/session-redis-failover.test.mts` checks them with real Redis servers and Sentinels. <a id="HY-115.19"></a> On Redis Cluster every command of the protocol has one key, so a session and its lock can live on different primaries; the PHP server speaks the protocol through `RedisClusterSessions`, because the `rediscluster` handler of phpredis takes no lock, and the Node and Python servers run through a cluster client. <a id="HY-115.20"></a> `tests/scripts/session-redis-cluster.test.mts` checks it on a real cluster of three primaries, also while a slot moves.

- **HY-58** <a id="HY-58.1"></a> A loader or an action may stop the request as a bad request. <a id="HY-58.2"></a> The server responds with status 400 and the text `Bad Request`, and runs no other loader or action of the request. <a id="HY-58.3"></a> An action may also return the route page with a stated status of 200, 409 or 422 and data: the server renders the route page with the route data merged with that data, as JSON for a JSON request and as a document otherwise, and responds with that status. <a id="HY-58.4"></a> Another status fails with HY-43. <a id="HY-58.5"></a> HY-26 is the page with status 422; a page with status 200 follows HY-52 and HY-53. <a id="HY-58.6"></a> Making a page with another status fails with the error `a page status`, a space, the status and ` is not 200, 409 or 422 (HY-58)`, of the classes of HY-46.2.

- **HY-69** <a id="HY-69.1"></a> A loader or an action may give the page of its request the status 403 with `Reply::status(403)` in PHP and `reply.status(403)` in Node and Python, for a page that shows other data in place of the data that the request may not see, such as a sign-in form in place of a page that needs a session. <a id="HY-69.2"></a> A page response that has status 200 otherwise, the page of a `GET` request or an action result page with status 200 (HY-58), then has status 403 and is rendered as it is with 200, as JSON for a JSON request and as a document otherwise. <a id="HY-69.3"></a> As every response with status 400 or more it has `Cache-Control: no-store` (HY-65), and as every response with another status than 200 it has no `ETag` and never receives 304 (HY-53). <a id="HY-69.4"></a> A page with status 409 or 422, a redirect, a stop and a failure keep their own status. <a id="HY-69.5"></a> Another status fails with HY-43, because 403 states that the request may not see the page; 401 would require a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge (RFC 9110), and 200 would state that the response is the page. <a id="HY-69.6"></a> A status that is not an integer of the data model (HY-52) fails with `TypeError` and the message `a page status of a reply is not an integer within ±(2^53 − 1) (HY-69)`, and another integer fails with the class of HY-46.2 and the message `page status <status> of a reply is not 403 (HY-69)`, where `<status>` is the integer in decimal digits.

- **HY-59** <a id="HY-59.1"></a> The application declares a body limit, the largest request body in bytes (8 MiB by default), and its form types, the media types of the request bodies that its actions and `/_hyper/keep` accept: one or both of `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and `multipart/form-data`, by default `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. <a id="HY-59.2"></a> Another limit or form type fails when the application opens. <a id="HY-59.3"></a> The server checks a request in this order, and runs no loader or action when a check fails:

  1. <a id="HY-59.4"></a> A body larger than the limit receives status 413 with the text `Content Too Large`, for every request and before HY-42. <a id="HY-59.5"></a> The size of a body is its length, or its `Content-Length` when that is larger, because PHP leaves the body empty when it is larger than `post_max_size`. <a id="HY-59.6"></a> The Node server stops reading a body when it passes the limit.
  2. <a id="HY-59.7"></a> After routing and HY-27, a `POST` request to an action or to `/_hyper/keep` whose `Content-Type` media type, without parameters and compared without case, is not a form type receives status 415 with the text `Unsupported Media Type`.
  3. <a id="HY-59.8"></a> Then the CSRF check of HY-24 answers 403.

  <a id="HY-59.9"></a> `App::run` of PHP fails before it answers when `post_max_size` is smaller than the limit, or when `multipart/form-data` is a form type and `enable_post_data_reading` is on (HY-57).

- **HY-60** <a id="HY-60.1"></a> The application may declare a response hook. <a id="HY-60.2"></a> The server calls it once for every response of the application with the request, the response and the elapsed time in milliseconds, including the responses that hyper answers itself: 400 (HY-42, HY-58), 403 (HY-24, HY-51), 404 and 405 (HY-27), 406 and the static shell (HY-62), the 400 and 406 of HY-116, the 400 of HY-127, the 400, 405 and 415 of HY-121, 413 and 415 (HY-59), and 500 (HY-43, HY-66). <a id="HY-60.3"></a> The request is the request as received, with the base path. <a id="HY-60.4"></a> The response is the response of the application with its `Content-Security-Policy` (HY-45); the session cookie that the session adds afterwards is not part of it. <a id="HY-60.5"></a> The elapsed time counts on a monotonic clock from the start of the request: `App::run` and `handle` of PHP take the start from their caller as an `hrtime(true)` value, such as the value that the first statement of a front controller takes, or count from their own call; the Node server counts with `performance.now()` from the time when `node:http` gives the request. <a id="HY-60.6"></a> No server subtracts a wall clock time such as `REQUEST_TIME_FLOAT` or `microtime(true)`, because an adjustment of the system time moves the wall clock backwards and gives a negative elapsed time. <a id="HY-60.7"></a> The Node server also reports the 400 and 431 responses to requests that `node:http` cannot parse, with a request of the method and the target of the request line, or with no request when the packet has no request line. <a id="HY-60.8"></a> The hook also receives the reply of the request (HY-52), so that it reads the values that the loaders and actions of the request decided: the reply that they received, also when the request ended with a stop (HY-50, HY-51, HY-58), a failure of HY-27 or an error of HY-43, and a new empty reply when the server answered before routing (HY-42, HY-59, a path without a route, `/_hyper/keep` and the responses that `node:http` cannot give to the application) or without a loader or an action (the 405 and 406 responses and the shell of HY-62, the 406 of HY-116 and every response of a representation, HY-121 and HY-122). <a id="HY-60.9"></a> A loader or an action records such a value with a note of the reply, a name and any value; a later note of the same name replaces the value and keeps its position. <a id="HY-60.10"></a> The server does not read the notes, and they are not part of the response. <a id="HY-60.11"></a> The hook also receives the failure of a 500 of HY-43 or HY-66, so that an application writes the cause with its own line: the message of the error of HY-43 (the message of a PHP `Throwable` or of a Node `Error`, or the text of another thrown value) or `the response to <method> <path> has <size> bytes, more than the response limit of <limit> bytes` of HY-66; for every other response it receives null. <a id="HY-60.12"></a> The files of the public directory of the Node server are not responses of the application. <a id="HY-60.13"></a> An error that the hook throws is not handled by HY-43; it reaches the caller of `handle`.

  - <a id="HY-60.14"></a> An error that escapes the answer of a request, because HY-43 does not handle it, is a failed read of the body, a failed stat of a file of the public directory, a failed session open or close, a failed write of the response, an error that the response hook throws, or an error that `around` raises outside `answer` (HY-97). <a id="HY-60.15"></a> The server logs it with the message of HY-43 and answers a plain 500 that hyper writes itself, identical in every adapter: status 500, the text `Internal Server Error`, `Cache-Control: no-store` (HY-65) and `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors <policy>` (HY-45). <a id="HY-60.16"></a> No server reports that 500 to the response hook. <a id="HY-60.17"></a> The write hook (HY-99) receives it once, with the request as the server received it. <a id="HY-60.18"></a> The request as received has the target, the headers and the cookies of the request; a body that was not read is empty, and its size is the Content-Length that the client declared. <a id="HY-60.19"></a> A request whose target the transport does not give (a WSGI environ without `RAW_URI` and `REQUEST_URI`, or an ASGI scope without `raw_path`) has no request to report, so no hook receives its 500. <a id="HY-60.20"></a> The 500 is written only when the response has not started. <a id="HY-60.21"></a> When the response has started, or the write of the 500 fails, the server closes the connection; a write that fails is reported to the write hook once, so no hook is called twice for a request. <a id="HY-60.22"></a> The WSGI and ASGI callables (HY-100) write the same 500 before their `start_response` or their first send. <a id="HY-60.23"></a> `App::run` writes the same 500 for an uncaught exception, through `set_exception_handler`, and for a fatal error of the request, which the shutdown function reads from `error_get_last()` as E_ERROR, E_CORE_ERROR, E_COMPILE_ERROR or E_USER_ERROR (a memory or time limit is an E_ERROR), when headers have not been sent.
  - <a id="HY-60.24"></a> The plain 500 of an escaped error keeps the response headers that the caller of hyper set before hyper received the request, and no other header. <a id="HY-60.25"></a> PHP keeps the headers of `headers_list()` at the call of `App::run`, and `sendReplacing` removes every other header and adds them again before the headers of the 500. <a id="HY-60.26"></a> Node writes the 500 with `writeHead` on the `node:http` response, which keeps a header that the caller set with `setHeader` before the listener of hyper ran. <a id="HY-60.27"></a> The WSGI and ASGI callables (HY-100) pass the 500 to the `start_response` or the `send` of their caller as any response.

  <a id="HY-60.28"></a> A note name that is not a string fails with `TypeError` and the message `a note name is not a string (HY-60)`. <a id="HY-60.29"></a> `notes()` returns the notes as a list of pairs of a name, which stays a string also when it is decimal, and its value, in the order of the first note of each name, in the three servers.

- **HY-65** <a id="HY-65.1"></a> Every response with a status of 400 or more has `Cache-Control: no-store`, so that no cache stores a failure: the plain text responses of HY-24, HY-27, HY-40, HY-42, HY-43, HY-51, HY-58, HY-59, HY-62, HY-66, HY-116, HY-127 and HY-121, the responses of a representation handler with such a status (HY-122), the plain 500 of an escaped error (HY-60), the 400 and 431 responses of the Node server to requests that `node:http` cannot parse (HY-60), the pages with status 409 or 422 (HY-58) and the pages with status 403 (HY-69). <a id="HY-65.2"></a> A reply does not change it (HY-52). <a id="HY-65.3"></a> Without the header, a cache may store a 404 or 405 response by its heuristic freshness (RFC 9111).

- **HY-66** <a id="HY-66.1"></a> The application declares a response limit, the largest response body in bytes (8 MiB by default); a limit that is not a positive integer fails when the application opens. <a id="HY-66.2"></a> The limit bounds the body that the server holds for sending one response, which a slow client keeps in the memory of the server process and of a web server that buffers the response. <a id="HY-66.3"></a> A response whose body is larger than the limit is not sent: the server writes `hyper: the response to <method> <path> has <size> bytes, more than the response limit of <limit> bytes` to its log, answers status 500 with the text `Internal Server Error` as HY-43 does, and reports that 500 to the response hook (HY-60) with the reply of the request. <a id="HY-66.4"></a> The size of a body is its length in bytes. <a id="HY-66.5"></a> The server renders a body completely before it compares its size, because the template programs render a document to one string.

- **HY-67** <a id="HY-67.1"></a> The application may declare a disconnect hook. <a id="HY-67.2"></a> The server calls it once, with the request as received, the elapsed milliseconds (HY-60) and the reply of the request, for a request whose client closed the connection before it received the complete response.

  - <a id="HY-67.3"></a> The Node server learns of the close when `node:http` reports that the connection closed before the response was written. <a id="HY-67.4"></a> It then runs no further loader, action or rendering of the request after the one that is running, writes no response, does not call the response hook and calls the disconnect hook.
  - <a id="HY-67.5"></a> PHP reports a closed connection only when a write to it fails, and a write of a small response to a closed connection can succeed. <a id="HY-67.6"></a> `App::run` turns `ignore_user_abort` off, so PHP ends the script at the first failed write of the response, and a shutdown function calls the disconnect hook when `connection_aborted()` is 1. <a id="HY-67.7"></a> The PHP server therefore renders the complete response and calls the response hook (HY-60) before it can detect the close, and it does not detect a close when every write of the response succeeds.
  - <a id="HY-67.8"></a> The Python server of `polyspec-hyper-server` (`create_server` of `polyspec.hyper.server`) learns of a closed connection only when a write of the response fails, as PHP does: `http.server` raises `BrokenPipeError`, `ConnectionResetError` or `ConnectionAbortedError` for a write to a connection that the client closed. <a id="HY-67.9"></a> The server renders the complete response and calls the response hook (HY-60) first, then writes the response; when a write fails with one of these errors, it writes no more of the response and calls the disconnect hook once with the request as received, the elapsed milliseconds and the reply of the request. <a id="HY-67.10"></a> It counts the elapsed time with `time.perf_counter_ns()`, a monotonic clock, from the time when its request handler starts the request, as it does for the response hook. <a id="HY-67.11"></a> It does not detect a close when every write of the response succeeds. <a id="HY-67.12"></a> `App.respond` answers a request as `App.handle` does and returns the response with the reply of the request, so that the server holds the reply that the disconnect hook receives; `App.handle` returns only the response.

- **HYC-9** <a id="HYC-9.1"></a> An error in the browser code is thrown from the htmx response hook. <a id="HYC-9.2"></a> htmx reports it with the `htmx:error` event and does not swap.

## Implementation equivalence

PHP, Python and TypeScript must satisfy the same declared protocol units, including manifest, request and file-limit rules (HY-1, HY-27, HY-114). CI runs declaration validation and cross-language equivalence in the entry `gates` of `ci.yml`, independently of language-specific, rendering and browser jobs. Each parity target runs exactly once; a failed parity target fails the entry `gates`, and so `ci-passed`, which a release requires of its run.

Each CI group owns its pinned tools, locked dependencies and build inputs. Language jobs install only the environments they execute. The protocol parity and browser integration groups independently prepare all implementations they compare and never consume another language job’s installation or build artifacts. Tool selection uses the shared `make install-tools TOOLS="..."` interface; package installation stays with npm, Composer and uv. Installation may download locked inputs; builds and checks remain offline. The selected installer is supplied by the pinned Kit release. npm is prepared by its separate bootstrap selector; PHP symbol extractors are installed explicitly through `make kit-install-symbols EXTRACTORS="php"` in the groups that execute them.

## Interface terms

A string is a text. A number is an integer or a float, as HY-54.8 reads a JSON number. A boolean is `true` or `false`. Null is the value `null`. A bigint is an integer of arbitrary size. Bytes is a byte sequence. A value is any value of the data model of HY-54. None is no result.
